Park Heath Park Useful Info Clubs and Societies Placement Support Student Academic Reps serve as a vital link between students and the school, university and Students' Union. Each programme across the university has Student Academic Reps, who are elected to represent their cohort on educational matters. Mae Cynrychiolwyr Academaidd Myfyrwyr yn gwasanaethu fel cyswllt hanfodol rhwng myfyrwyr a'r ysgol, y brifysgol ac Undeb y Myfyrwyr. Mae gan bob rhaglen ar draws y brifysgol Gynrychiolwyr Academaidd Myfyrwyr, sy'n cael eu hethol i gynrychioli eu carfan ar faterion addysgol. How the Rep system works Sut mae’r system Cynrychiolwyr yn gweithio? The Academic Rep System The Student Voice team in the Students' Union work closely with the university to ensure that the Student Academic Representation system works, that students have regular opportunities to provide feedback, and that Reps are supported effectively. Student Staff Panels The main role of a Rep is to listen to feedback from their peers and take this forward for discussion with staff members at regular Student Staff Panels. These are meetings designed to facilitate constructive conversation between Reps and school staff. Working with the University Reps also work closely with university staff to find solutions to ongoing issues, and to help feed this back to the cohort. Reps are not expected to deal with any issues that are not academic or related directly to their programme of study. Working with Student Voice Reps work closely with the Student Voice team in the Students' Union, attending appropriate training, receiving regular newsletters, and joining in with additional opportunities. Take a look at our Frequently Asked Questions to find out more about the Rep role or contact StudentReps@cardiff.ac.uk . Who is my Student Academic Rep? Pwy yw fy Nghynrychiolydd Academaidd Myfyrwyr? Do you have some feedback and want to know who your Student Academic Rep is? Click the Find my Rep button below to find and contact your Student Rep. You will need to log in to use Find my Rep. Oes gennych chi adborth ac eisiau gwybod pwy yw eich Cynrychiolydd Academaidd Myfyrwyr? Cliciwch y botwm Dod o Hyd i Fy Nghynrychiolydd isod i ddod o hyd i’ch Cynrychiolydd Myfyrwyr a chysylltu ag ef/hi. Bydd angen i chi fewngofnodi i ddefnyddio Dod o Hyd i'm Cynrychiolydd. Find My Rep Dod o hyd i fy nghynrychiolydd Frequently Asked Questions Cwestiynau cyffredin If you are interested in becoming a Student Academic Representative, or if you are interested in learning a bit more about what they do, look at our frequently asked questions below. Os oes gennych ddiddordeb mewn dod yn Gynrychiolydd Academaidd Myfyrwyr, neu os oes gennych ddiddordeb mewn dysgu ychydig mwy am yr hyn maen nhw'n ei wneud, edrychwch ar ein cwestiynau cyffredin isod. If you would like to discuss any aspects of the role with the Student Voice team, contact StudentReps@cardiff.ac.uk . Os hoffech drafod unrhyw agweddau ar y rôl gyda thîm Llais y Myfyrwyr, cysylltwch â StudentReps@cardiff.ac.uk . What is a Student Academic Representative? Beth yw Cynrychiolydd Academaidd Myfyrwyr? Every programme has a Student Academic Rep to represent the views of their cohort. Within the 24 schools at Cardiff University, this means over 1000 Reps every year across the organisation. Reps bridge the gap between students and staff members, gathering relevant feedback, raising it at meetings, and reporting back on any outcomes. Mae gan bob rhaglen Gynrychiolydd Academaidd Myfyrwyr i gynrychioli barn eu carfan. O fewn 24 ysgol ym Mhrifysgol Caerdydd, mae hyn yn golygu dros 1000 o Gynrychiolwyr ar draws y sefydliad bob blwyddyn. Mae cynrychiolwyr yn pontio’r bwlch rhwng myfyrwyr ac aelodau staff, gan gasglu adborth perthnasol, ei godi mewn cyfarfodydd, ac adrodd yn ôl ar unrhyw ganlyniadau. What types of issues do Student Academic Reps deal with? Pa fathau o faterion y mae Cynrychiolwyr Academaidd Myfyrwyr yn delio â nhw? Student Academic Reps are elected to speak on behalf of their cohorts’ educational concerns. This means they deal with issues or problems that arise regarding the course (including assessments and feedback, module content, or timetabling). They are not expected to deal with any wellbeing concerns or personal matters relating to students on their course. However, they will be able to signpost students with such concerns to appropriate university services. Mae Cynrychiolwyr Academaidd Myfyrwyr yn cael eu hethol i siarad ar ran pryderon addysgol eu carfannau. Mae hyn yn golygu eu bod yn delio â materion neu broblemau sy’n codi ynghylch y cwrs (gan gynnwys asesiadau ac adborth, cynnwys modiwlau, neu amserlennu). Nid oes disgwyl iddynt ddelio ag unrhyw bryderon lles na materion personol sy’n ymwneud â myfyrwyr ar eu cwrs. Fodd bynnag, byddant yn gallu cyfeirio myfyrwyr sydd â phryderon o'r fath at wasanaethau prifysgol priodol. How do I find the Student Academic Rep for my school? Sut mae dod o hyd i’r Cynrychiolydd Academaidd Myfyrwyr ar gyfer fy ysgol? Your Student Academic Rep should make themselves known to you in the first few weeks of the year. You can also find the details of your Rep by filtering by your college, school, and year in the Find My Rep widget above. Dylai eich Cynrychiolydd Academaidd Myfyrwyr gyflwyno ei hunain yn ystod wythnosau cyntaf y flwyddyn. Gallwch hefyd ddod o hyd i fanylion eich Cynrychiolydd drwy hidlo yn ôl eich coleg, ysgol, a blwyddyn yn y teclyn Dod o Hyd i Fy Nghynrychiolydd uchod. Where does feedback go? I ble mae adborth yn mynd? The university has a comprehensive committee structure that is designed to ensure that all feedback can be resolved or discussed at the appropriate level. Any feedback that is passed onto Student Academic Representatives will be raised with school staff at a Student Staff Panel meeting. Depending on the nature of the issue, the panel of staff and students may find a solution, which will then be communicated back to students. If no solution can be found, the issue will be allocated to another appropriate committee, who will work towards an outcome. Mae gan y brifysgol strwythur pwyllgor cynhwysfawr sydd wedi’i gynllunio i sicrhau y gellir datrys neu drafod yr holl adborth ar y lefel briodol. Bydd unrhyw adborth a drosglwyddir i Gynrychiolwyr Academaidd Myfyrwyr yn cael ei godi gyda staff yr ysgol mewn cyfarfod Panel Staff Myfyrwyr. Yn dibynnu ar natur y mater, gall y panel o staff a myfyrwyr ddod o hyd i ateb, a fydd wedyn yn cael ei gyfleu'n ôl i'r myfyrwyr. Os na ellir dod o hyd i ateb, bydd y mater yn cael ei ddyrannu i bwyllgor priodol arall, a fydd yn gweithio tuag at ganlyniad. What is a Student Staff Panel? Beth yw Panel Staff Myfyrwyr? Student Staff Panels are meetings that occur between Student Academic Representatives and staff within the school. These happen once per semester and exist to ensure that there is an effective dialogue between staff and students. These are led by a student Chair and Vice-Chair, and facilitation is supported by school staff. Any outcomes from Student Staff Panel meetings should be communicated with all students. Mae Paneli Staff Myfyrwyr yn gyfarfodydd sy'n digwydd rhwng Cynrychiolwyr Academaidd Myfyrwyr a staff o fewn ysgol. Mae'r rhain yn digwydd unwaith y semester ac yn bodoli i sicrhau bod deialog effeithiol rhwng staff a myfyrwyr. Mae'r rhain yn cael eu harwain gan Gadeirydd ac Is-gadeirydd myfyrwyr a’u hwyluso gan staff yr ysgol. Dylid cyfleu unrhyw ganlyniadau o gyfarfodydd Panel Staff Myfyrwyr i bob myfyriwr. What is a College Forum? Beth yw Fforwm Coleg? College Forums are meetings facilitated by the Students’ Union and provide an opportunity for Reps to report issues that cannot be resolved at a Student Staff Panel. These are split by college and are chaired by a Sabbatical Officer. The Chair and Vice-Chair of each Student Staff Panel will be invited to attend and provide an update on the items discussed at their latest meeting. College Deans and professional service staff will also be in attendance, so if there is any feedback that is not suitable for a Student Staff Panel, it can be raised at a College Forum. Mae Fforymau Coleg yn gyfarfodydd a hwylusir gan Undeb y Myfyrwyr ac maent yn rhoi cyfle i Gynrychiolwyr adrodd ar faterion na ellir eu datrys mewn Panel Staff Myfyrwyr. Mae'r rhain wedi'u rhannu yn ôl coleg ac yn cael eu cadeirio gan Swyddog Sabothol. Gwahoddir Cadeirydd ac Is-gadeirydd pob Panel Staff Myfyrwyr i fynychu a rhoi'r wybodaeth ddiweddaraf am yr eitemau a drafodwyd yn eu cyfarfod diweddaraf. Bydd Deoniaid Coleg a staff gwasanaeth proffesiynol hefyd yn bresennol, felly os oes unrhyw adborth nad yw'n addas ar gyfer Panel Staff Myfyrwyr, gellir ei godi mewn Fforwm Coleg. Why should I volunteer Pam ddylwn i wirfoddoli? Becoming a Student Academic Representative is a great opportunity. Not only can you represent your cohort and gain an insight into the workings of your school, you will also gain lots of transferable skills that will look great on your CV. As a Rep, you will receive regular communication from the Students’ Union with additional opportunities. You can also get a certificate at the end of the year! Mae dod yn Gynrychiolydd Academaidd Myfyrwyr yn gyfle gwych. A fydda i’n derbyn hyfforddiant a chefnogaeth? As a Student Academic Representative, you will receive comprehensive training from the Student Voice team about your role. This will take you through what to expect from your role, and the support you can access. Each school has different ways of doing this, so it is a good idea to get in touch with your Student Rep Coordinator and see what methods have been successful for previous Reps. Gweithio What are College Forums? The Students’ Union holds College Forums, to give Student Academic Representatives the opportunity to discuss feedback with the elected Sabbatical Officers and senior university staff. Who attends College Forums? The Chair and Vice-Chair of each Student Staff Panel are invited to attend, to provide an update of what was discussed at their last meeting, and raise any issues that cannot be resolved by school staff. If a problem cannot be resolved at a Student Staff Panel, it can be brought to a College Forum. What happens in a College Forum? Student Academic Representatives across the college will have an opportunity to speak on behalf of their school. Sabbatical Officers chair the meetings, and support students to engage in conversation with the college Deans, and representatives from other professional services. Sharing best practice As well as raising concerns, this is a really good opportunity for Chairs to share best practice in their college. They can share ideas and solutions to common problems with their peers. College Forum Dates Dyddiadau Fforwm y Coleg Each Chair and Vice-Chair will be automatically invited to the College Forums by the Student Voice Team. If you are a Rep and would like to attend a College Forum, or you have any questions, please email the Student Voice Team StudentReps@cardiff.ac.uk . It is a large forum where a wide variety of students come to debate and determine the direction of Cardiff Students’ Union. Mae’n fforwm mawr lle mae amrywiaeth eang o fyfyrwyr yn dod i drafod a phenderfynu ar gyfeiriad Undeb Myfyrwyr Caerdydd. Any student can attend the AGM and have their say on the items discussed. The Union is a transparent organisation which is run by the student population. This is a great opportunity to have a hands-on impact on the democracy and running of the Students’ Union. Gall unrhyw fyfyriwr fynychu’r Cyfarfod Cyffredinol Blynyddol a dweud eu dweud ar yr eitemau a drafodir. Mae’r Undeb yn sefydliad tryloyw sy’n cael ei redeg gan boblogaeth y myfyrwyr. The Union's AGM plays a crucial role in the governance processes of the Union. It sees hundreds of students come together to debate and vote on a series of motions which will determine the campaigning work of the Elected Officers . It also sees students receive the financial accounts of the Union from the previous financial year, approve the affiliation of the Union to organisations like BUCS , and ask questions to the Board of Trustees . Mae CCB yr Undeb yn chwarae rhan hanfodol ym mhrosesau llywodraethu’r Undeb. Sut ydw i’n cyflwyno cynnig? Motions for change can be submitted by any student. A motion consists of an idea that you think the Union should follow. To find out more about how to write a motion check out our Motion Submission Guidance and Procedure Document . Gall unrhyw fyfyriwr gyflwyno cynigion ar gyfer newid. Mae cynnig yn cynnwys syniad yr ydych chi’n credu y dylai’r Undeb ei ddilyn. I gael gwybod mwy am sut i ysgrifennu cynnig, edrychwch ar ein Dogfen Canllawiau a Gweithdrefn Cyflwyno Cynigion . Students have the opportunity during a specific period ahead of the meeting to submit motions they want to be considered at the AGM. Submissions should be made through the AGM Motion Submission Portal Mae gan fyfyrwyr y cyfle, yn ystod cyfnod penodol cyn y cyfarfod, i gyflwyno cynigion y maent am iddynt eu hystyried yn y Cyfarfod Cyffredinol Blynyddol. Dylid gwneud cyflwyniadau trwy Borth Cyflwyno Cynigion y Cyfarfod Cyffredinol Blynyddol . Once submitted, motions will be reviewed to ensure they are within the power of the AGM. Any motions considered to be within the powers of the AGM will then be put to a vote by students via a priority ballot. This priority ballot will determine which motions get to be debated at the AGM, with only the top 4 motions making it onto the agenda. Any motion which does not make it into the top 4 but receives at least 25 votes will be submitted to Student Senate for consideration, as long as it within their remit. Students will be notified when the priority ballot opens so they can vote for the motions they want to see debated. The final agenda for the meeting will be made available 7 days before the AGM. Bydd myfyrwyr yn cael gwybod pan fydd y bleidlais flaenoriaeth yn agor fel y gallant bleidleisio dros y cynigion y maent am eu gweld yn cael eu trafod. If you are unable to attend the meeting but still want your voice heard and your vote counted, you can have another student attend as your proxy. That means that another individual attends in your place, speaks and votes on your behalf. Os na allwch fynychu’r cyfarfod ond eich bod chi eisiau i’ch llais gael ei glywed a’ch pleidlais gael ei chyfrif, gallwch chi gael myfyriwr arall i fynychu fel eich dirprwy. Mae hynny’n golygu bod unigolyn arall yn mynychu yn eich lle, yn siarad ac yn pleidleisio ar eich rhan. To appoint a proxy you simply fill in the 'Appointment of Proxy' form. Sports and Societies AGM voted to stop minimum memberships for sports clubs and societies being raised to 30. Access to facilities AGM voted to ensure the Great Hall didn't become a full-time lecture theatre, maintaining availability of the space to student groups. Any student can submit a motion for discussion and run to be a Student Senator. The Senate has authority to make and review policy, ensuring the SU’s work aligns with our students’ values. Policies passed by Student Senate are the framework within which the Union and its Elected Officers operate. Corff llunio polisïau Undeb y Myfyrwyr yw Senedd y Myfyrwyr, ochr yn ochr â'r Cyfarfod Cyffredinol Blynyddol a'r Refferenda. Gall unrhyw fyfyriwr gyflwyno cynnig i'w drafod ac ymgeisio i fod yn Seneddwr Myfyrwyr. Mae gan y Senedd yr awdurdod i lunio ac adolygu polisi, gan sicrhau bod gwaith Undeb y Myfyrwyr yn cyd-fynd â gwerthoedd ein myfyrwyr. Polisïau a basiwyd gan Senedd y Myfyrwyr yw'r fframwaith y mae'r Undeb a'i Swyddogion Etholedig yn gweithredu ynddo. How does it work? Sut mae’n gweithio? Membership Student Senate has over 50 student members and is made up of elected Student Senators, Sabbatical Officers, Campaign Officers, randomly selected Student Academic Representatives, and randomly selected students. This helps ensure that Student Senate is as representative of the general student body as possible. Responsibilities Student Senate has a range of responsibilities which include noting the Union’s budget, receiving reports from the trustees, working with the Board of Trustees to approve the Union’s governing documents, and voting on the policies put forward by students. Creating policies To put forward policy, all you have to do is submit an idea on our Ideas Platform or vote on existing ideas. You can 'up vote' or 'down vote' ideas. If a 'down vote' is received, that means the total number will go down i.e. if you have 0 votes and someone 'down votes' it will become -1 votes. Debating and deciding Student Senate will then debate the idea and vote to decide if it will become Students' Union policy. If your idea has an operational component (for example, "the Students' Union should serve more vegan-friendly options"), it may not need to be discussed at Student Senate, and instead may be better achieved by providing feedback directly to our Sales and Customer Services team. If you would like to talk about an idea further, contact Democracy@cardiff.ac.uk . Park Heath Park Useful Info Clubs and Societies Placement Support How does the Accountability Panel work? Sut mae’r Panel Atebolrwydd yn gweithio? Who attends Each Sabbatical Officer Executive Committee sends two representatives along to the Accountability Panel meetings. The Accountability Panel also has a separate Chair and Vice-Chair. What the panel does The Accountability Panel has responsibility for ensuring that all Sabbatical Officers fulfil their role commitments, including implementing the policies they lead on, and delivering the manifesto commitments that led to their election. Outcomes The outcomes from the Accountability Panel will be published below. What powers does the Accountability Panel have? Pa bwerau sydd gan y Panel Atebolrwydd? The Accountability Panel has the power to award notices to the Sabbatical Officers, either in recognition of outstanding work, or when they want to see improvements. Mae gan y Panel Atebolrwydd y pŵer i ddyfarnu hysbysiadau i'r Swyddogion Sabothol, naill ai i gydnabod gwaith rhagorol, neu pan fyddant am weld gwelliannau. A Notice of Satisfaction is considered when the Panel wish to formally recognise a Sabbatical Officer for outstanding work in relation to their role, responsibilities, and manifesto commitments. A Notice of Required Improvement is considered when the Panel is dissatisfied in a Sabbatical Officer’s work or conduct. The Panel may also consider a more severe motion of censure when they believe the Sabbatical Officer has committed a serious offence against their office or democratic responsibilities. Ystyrir Hysbysiad Bodlonrwydd pan fydd y Panel yn dymuno cydnabod Swyddog Sabothol yn ffurfiol am waith rhagorol mewn perthynas â'u rôl, cyfrifoldebau ac ymrwymiadau maniffesto. Ystyrir Hysbysiad o Welliant Angenrheidiol pan fydd y Panel yn anfodlon â gwaith neu ymddygiad Swyddog Sabothol. Gall y Panel hefyd ystyried cynnig mwy difrifol o gerydd pan fyddant yn credu bod y Swyddog Sabothol wedi cyflawni trosedd difrifol yn erbyn eu swydd neu gyfrifoldebau democrataidd. Is the process the same for Campaign Officers? A yw'r broses yr un fath ar gyfer Swyddogion Ymgyrch? Due to the different nature of their roles, Campaign Officers follow an alternative accountability process. Instead of interacting with the Accountability Panel, all Campaign Officers provide verbal reports to the Student Senate throughout the year. Oherwydd natur wahanol eu rolau, mae Swyddogion Ymgyrch yn dilyn proses atebolrwydd gwahanol. Yn lle rhyngweithio â'r Panel Atebolrwydd, mae pob Swyddog Ymgyrch yn darparu adroddiadau llafar i Senedd y Myfyrwyr drwy gydol y flwyddyn. How do I see what was discussed at the sessions? Sut alla i weld beth a drafodwyd yn y sesiynau? The minutes will be published on the Students' Union website following each meeting. This will include a record of any notices or motions received by an Officer. Cyhoeddir y cofnodion ar wefan Undeb y Myfyrwyr yn dilyn pob cyfarfod. Bydd hyn yn cynnwys cofnod o unrhyw hysbysiadau neu gynigion a dderbyniwyd gan Swyddog. How can I get involved? Sut alla i gymryd rhan? Only members of Executive Committees will be invited to join the Accountability Panel. If you are interested in participating in an Executive Committee, you can find more information here . Dim ond aelodau o Bwyllgorau Gweithredol fydd yn cael gwahoddiad i ymuno â'r Panel Atebolrwydd. Os oes gennych ddiddordeb mewn cymryd rhan mewn Pwyllgor Gweithredol, gallwch ddod o hyd i ragor o wybodaeth yma . Park Useful Info Clubs and Societies Placement Support Cardiff University and the Students' Union have different types of policy. University policies are created by University staff with input from student representatives, including Sabbatical Officers, and cover areas like campus spaces, lecture recordings, and support services. Students' Union policies - proposed and passed by students - define how the Union and its Officers operate. These policies may set rules for the Union or mandate Officers to lobby the University for change. Mae gan Brifysgol Caerdydd ac Undeb y Myfyrwyr wahanol fathau o bolisïau. Mae polisïau'r brifysgol yn cael eu creu gan staff y Brifysgol gyda mewnbwn gan gynrychiolwyr myfyrwyr, gan gynnwys Swyddogion Sabothol, ac maent yn cwmpasu meysydd fel mannau ar y campws, recordiadau darlithoedd, a gwasanaethau cymorth. Mae polisïau Undeb y Myfyrwyr - a gynigir ac a basiwyd gan fyfyrwyr - yn diffinio sut mae'r Undeb a'i Swyddogion yn gweithredu. Gall y polisïau hyn osod rheolau ar gyfer yr Undeb neu orfodi Swyddogion i lobïo'r Brifysgol am newid. How is Students' Union policy created? Sut mae polisi Undeb y Myfyrwyr yn cael ei greu? As a Students' Union we engage with you, our students, on issues that are affecting you. With your responses and feedback, we work with you and your elected representatives to refine written definitions and actions. Fel Undeb Myfyrwyr rydym yn ymgysylltu â chi, ein myfyrwyr, ar faterion sy'n effeithio arnoch chi. Gyda'ch ymatebion a'ch adborth, rydym yn gweithio gyda chi a'ch cynrychiolwyr etholedig i fireinio diffiniadau a chamau ysgrifenedig. Student Senate , AGM , and Referenda are all examples of how we use our representative and democratic structures to ensure the policies you want happen. Mae Senedd y Myfyrwyr , CCB , a Refferenda i gyd yn enghreifftiau o sut rydym yn defnyddio ein strwythurau cynrychioliadol a democrataidd i sicrhau bod y polisïau rydych chi eu heisiau yn digwydd. What should I do if I have an idea? Beth ddylwn i ei wneud os oes gen i syniad? Cardiff Students' Union is a student-led organisation. This means big or small, practical or political, whatever the nature of your idea we want to hear about it! Mae Undeb Myfyrwyr Caerdydd yn sefydliad dan arweiniad myfyrwyr. Mae hyn yn golygu mawr neu fach, ymarferol neu wleidyddol, beth bynnag yw natur eich syniad, rydym am glywed amdano! If you want some help or advice formulating your idea, feel free to contact the Student Voice team. Sometimes you might have an idea that is of a more practical/operational nature. We want to hear all about these ideas too! Os ydych chi eisiau rhywfaint o help neu gyngor i lunio'ch syniad, mae croeso i chi gysylltu â thîm Llais y Myfyrwyr. Weithiau efallai bod gennych chi syniad sydd o natur fwy ymarferol/weithredol. Rydyn ni eisiau clywed am y syniadau hyn hefyd! If you would like to submit a policy to student senate or AGM, please do! The Student Voice team is more than happy to help you in the formation of your policy submission. Remember, policy lapses after three years. Mae ein Llyfr Polisïau, a geir isod, yn cynnwys yr holl bolisïau cyfredol sydd ar waith. Os hoffech gyflwyno polisi i senedd y myfyrwyr neu'r Cyfarfod Cyffredinol Blynyddol, gwnewch hynny! Mae tîm Llais y Myfyrwyr yn fwy na pharod i'ch helpu i lunio'ch cyflwyniad polisi. Policy passed Polisi wedi'i basio All AGM Senate Year November 2025 November 2024 November 2023 Year Academic Year 2025-26 Academic Year 2024-25 Academic Year 2023-24 Academic Year 2022-23 It’s Taken Long Enough: It’s Time To Act on Sexual Violence AGM Resolves 1. The Students’ Union elected officers must lobby Cardiff University to publicly acknowledge failings to protect and support survivors of sexual misconduct. 2. The Students’ Union must provide consent and bystander training for all sports clubs, societies and student media groups. This must be a mandatory requirement for all groups to attend and that there will be repercussions for lack of engagement. 2.1. This training should not be limited just to these groups and their committees but should be readily available to all students who wish to engage in this. 2.2. This training should include, but not be limited to: Discussing the pyramid of sexual violence e.g. how rape ‘jokes’ contributes to sexual violence. How to ask for consent Stealthing Sharking Coercive control How to be an effective bystander Head pushing Asphyxiation 2.3. All of this training should use translatable examples which reflect everyday student life. 3. Lets Talk Consent campaign set up by Georgia Spry (AU President 2023-25) must be taken on by elected officers each year to coincide with Freshers Week. 4. The Sabbatical Officers must implement the new ‘Fit to Stand’ requirement for new election candidates. They should ensure appropriate collaboration with the University to ensure necessary information is shared and undertake consultation with Time to Act and students on these requirements. 5. The working group set up within the Students’ Union due to the Time To Act motion in 2023 must be taken up by the president and women's officer each year. The membership of this working group must be updated each year. 6. The Students’ Union elected officers must collect and publish data on the prevalence of sexual misconduct at Cardiff University each year. This should include a consultation which is sent electronically to all members of the Union. The Students’ Union should also hold engagement events for students to come and ask questions about the proposed consultation. 7. The Students’ Union officers must commit to a student-led review into SSIT and Student Cases. This review will be led by the Sabbatical Officers and will be open to students to contribute. 8. The Students’ Union should look in partnership with Cardiff University, review and if feasible, introduce, strengthened safeguarding, investigation, and disciplinary measures relating to cases of sexual misconduct. This review should include consideration of how precautionary and punitive measures are applied to ensure consistency, fairness and student safety. 9. The Students’ Union officers must lobby the university to further update the student conduct procedure specifically around sexual violence. This must include the following: Survivors must not be forced to be in the panel room with their alleged perpetrator. Procedures must treat survivors as such rather than putting them on trial. Survivors must be treated with dignity and respect. Survivors going through this procedure must be aware of trauma-informed independent specialist bodies or representatives such as New Pathways. This procedure must be independent 10. The Students’ Union elected officers must work to highlight the impact sexual violence has on marginalised communites by working with organisations such as BAWSO and Galop. 11. The Students’ Union to provide practical support for and flag additional external support to students who are trapped in living situations with their abuser. This support should include: Finding alternative placement for victims. Signposting survivors towards Refuge who provide emergency temporary housing. Offering support with housing applications to the local authority. Offering wellbeing support tailored towards students who are housed with their perpetrator. 12. The Students’ Union elected officers should lobby the housing letting agents in Cardiff for example Cardiff Students Letting, CPS, John Winters, Unite etc. to add a clause to rental contracts allowing victims to break their lease without penalties or repercussions if they live with their perpetrator and should help them find alternative accommodation. 13. The Students’ Union to have greater measures to flag support given by Stronger Together by working with the student group and actively promoting this to students when engaging in campaigns around sexual violence. Proposed by Rebecca Rumsey Passed by AGM 20/11/2025 My Scrubs, My Choice: Equality in Healthcare Dress Code AGM Resolves 1. That the Students’ Union lobby the University and its healthcare schools to introduce a framework allowing students to confidentially discuss and request accommodations for modesty requirements, either via email or an online portal. 2. That the Students’ Union lobby the University and healthcare schools to provide industry-standard, alternative modest uniform and scrub options - including elbow-length sleeve scrubs, disposable forearm sleeves, skirt scrubs, and theatre-approved religious head coverings for surgical placements - in line with NHS guidance. 3. That the Students’ Union advocates to the University’s healthcare schools for the adoption of NHS-approved alternatives for modest clothing within theatre and placement settings. 4. That the Students’ Union lobbies the University to commit to regular Equality Impact Assessments of healthcare uniform policies, in line with NHS guidance. 5. The Students’ Union works with the University to ensure that healthcare uniforms and scrubs fall in line with the goals of the University’s Strategic Equality Plan 2024-2028. 6. The Students’ Union to update its equality and inclusivity communications to reaffirm students’ freedom of choice in clothing, including religious and modest dress, as part of its commitment to equality and bodily autonomy. 7. That the Students’ Union work closely with the local health board to achieve the above resolutions in a practical manner for healthcare students. Proposed by Zohaib Tahir Passed by AGM 20/11/2025 For Cardiff Students' Union to campaign for and support Pro-Choice AGM Resolves 1. Reaffirmation of Stance – Cardiff Students’ Union’s Elected Officer will publicly reaffirm its support for pro-choice 2. Accurate and Inclusive Language – The SU will maintain unbiased, medically accurate, and inclusive terminology relating to pregnancy, abortion, and reproductive health, expanding information on miscarriage support and policy. 3. Accessible, Up-to-Date Information – The SU will retain and regularly review balanced links to reliable, current information on pregnancy, abortion, and healthcare services. 4. Confidential Access to Support – The SU will display up-to-date information about pregnancy and abortion services on toilet stall doors, ensuring private access for students in vulnerable or abusive situations. 5. Sabbatical Officers Leadership – The Sabbatical Officers will remain responsible for ensuring SU campaigns and strategies actively support the pro-choice stance and a safe, inclusive environment. 6. Awareness Campaigns – The Sabbatical Officers, with the Campaign Officers, will continue pro-choice awareness campaigns promoting access to safe, legal abortion and accurate information. 8. Partnership with the University – The SU and Cardiff University will collaborate on a working group to ensure students understand their rights to bodily autonomy and reproductive healthcare, including abortion. 9. Protection from Harassment and Misinformation – The SU Elected Officers will condemn and speak out against anti-choice organisations that harass or intimidate students and/or spread misinformation. 10. Support for Targeted Students – The SU will evaluate and strengthen support services for students affected by anti-choice activity, ensuring proactive measures to protect wellbeing. 11. Continued Progress and Review – The SU will build on its current progress, striving to maintain and advance a campus environment grounded in clarity, compassion, accurate information, and the right to choose. Proposed by Eve Chamberlain Passed by AGM 20/11/2025 Making Cardiff a Safe Space for Trans Students AGM Resolves 1. Reaffirm and Strengthen the SU’s Commitment to Trans Inclusion. Cardiff Students’ Union Elected Officers will publicly reaffirm their commitment to trans rights and trans inclusion. 2. Improve Visibility and Access to Trans-Inclusive Facilities 2.1. The SU will work with Cardiff University to Expand the availability of gender-neutral toilets and changing facilities, prioritising sports facilities such as Talybont. Ensure all toilets include appropriate hygiene waste bins. Improve resources about gender-neutral and inclusive spaces. Ensure trans students are able to use the spaces and facilities they’re most comfortable using. Publicise Trans Support Services and Safe Spaces 2.2. The SU will collaborate with the University to: Increase awareness of the LGBTQ+ and gender-diverse safe spaces through resources. Clearly promote the process for changing names and gender markers on university systems, including student ID cards, records, and the SU website. Ensure there is support for trans students on a year abroad especially in less trans-inclusive countries. Ensure Consistency in Respecting Students’ Identities 2.3. The SU will lobby Cardiff University to implement a university-wide standard ensuring all departments, systems, and staff use students’ chosen names and pronouns in all communications and records, being mindful of those who use alternative names/pronouns with designated people. 3. Trans Inclusion in Sport 3.1. The VP Sports will: Work with BUCS, the Athletic Union, and relevant sports bodies to ensure trans students can participate in sports without discrimination, regardless of identity. Provide training to club committees on trans inclusion and awareness. Campaign for national sports governing bodies to revise discriminatory policies that limit trans athlete participation. 4. Education and Awareness Campaigns. The Sabbatical Officers and LGBTQ+ Officers will lead annual campaigns promoting trans inclusion and awareness, addressing misinformation and celebrating trans identities. These campaigns will include educational materials for all students and training opportunities for societies and student leaders. 5. Oppose Conversion Therapy. The SU will continue to condemn all forms of conversion therapy for all trans and LGBTQ+ identities and will lobby the Welsh Government and UK Government to implement a comprehensive, national ban on conversion practices. 6. Strengthen Reporting and Support Mechanisms 6.1. The SU will work with the University to ensure that: Reporting mechanisms for transphobic harassment are visible, accessible, and trusted. It is made clear that transphobia is not tolerated under any circumstances. Students who experience transphobia are supported through welfare services and peer-led networks. 7. Representation and Consultation The SU will ensure trans students are meaningfully consulted in all decisions affecting their wellbeing and representation, including through trans-led advisory groups or focus panels. 8. Monitoring and Accountability. The SU will review progress on these commitments annually, with the Sabbatical Officers reporting to Student Senate and publishing updates on the SU website. 9. Condemn All Forms of Transphobia. The students union will not condone any form of transphobia and will deal with any reports of it accordingly. Proposed by Eve Chamberlain Passed by AGM 20/11/2025 Securing Justice: A Renewed Call to End Sexual Violence AGM Resolves 1. Cardiff Students’ Union Officers should make and take preventative measures to protect victims of sexual misconduct, we recommend that this is done by working with other organisations such as ‘Our streets Now’ and campaigns (which are yearly or biyearly reviewed) promoting consent around both Cathays and Heath Campus. 1a. The campaigns could include information on support offered to victims, what consent is, healthy relationships etc. 2. Cardiff Students’ Union Officers should lobby the University to implement Bystander training for all staff members, as well as promote it to students yearly, through numerous platforms; such as but not limited to enrolment, society and sports clubs committee training, university intranet pages, posters. Cardiff Students’ Union Officers should also work to implement such training for all staff members in the Students’ Union. 3. Cardiff Students’ Union Officers and Cardiff University should publicly acknowledge possible failings of protecting and supporting previous victims of sexual misconduct. 4. Cardiff Students’ Union Officers and Cardiff University should provide better information around healthy relationships through posters, informative videos, training to societies/sports clubs and pages on the student intranet page. 4a. These informative posters should be made in line with Women’s Aid Survivors handbook on health relationships 4b. These informative posters should also be made with awareness of current student culture, particularly surrounding dating and relationships. We recommend this is done by questionnaires and reviews of what students want to see. 5. Cardiff Students’ Union Officers and Cardiff university should promote the fact that “Coercion is not consent” and that consent is not in relation to the relationship the victim has with their perpetrator. 6. Cardiff Students’ Union Officers should aggressively lobby the university to promote its support offered to victims 7. The Cardiff Students’ Union Officers and Cardiff University should acknowledge the fact that healthcare students are particularly vulnerable to sexual misconduct on their placements. In response the Students Union and Cardiff University should ensure that students on placement can report the incident, change placement locations and are offered numerous forms of support. Students should also be continuously informed that reporting will have no impact on their academic progression 8. The Students’ Union and Cardiff University should advertise SSIT better, this should be followed by a questionnaire of different ways students wish to see it promoted. 9. The University should have more security and safety measures to protect students on Cathays and Heath campus from sexual misconduct, particularly following the recent assault of a woman under Senghenydd bridge. Conduct a student-led review into the disclosure response team following on from the ideas set up by Emily Carr, SU’s Women’s Officer (2022/23). 4.6. Ensure that cases of harassment and discrimination are thoroughly investigated and ensure just outcomes for the victim, including criminal convictions, and permanent expulsions. Passed by Senate 11/12/2025 Campaign for a Sustainable, Biodiverse and Globally Responsible University: taking decisive action in the face of the climate and nature crises, together. Submitted by Liliana Tarrant Snedden Motion Resolves: 1. The Sabbatical and Campaign Officers lobby the University to incorporate the UN Sustainable Development Goals and the principles of the Well-Being of Future Generations (Wales) Act 2015 within all decision making. Campaigning to ensure the University adheres to its current Environmental and Sustainability Plan (2025-2035). Including a particular focus on minimising environmental harms and reducing respective carbon footprints. 2. The Sabbatical and Campaign Officers lobby the university to commit to clear actions under the four key headings, detailed below: 2.1. A commitment to renewable energy, environmental sustainability, and the  protection and improvement of biodiversity. 2.1.1. The further development and implementation of strategy to decarbonise Cardiff University properties as soon as possible. Achieving this could involve the use of renewables, energy storage technologies and measures to reduce energy demand such as insulation. This could also involve educating building users, including staff and students, to prevent energy waste. 2.1.2.  A public commitment to ethical investment, where investments and banking practices are conducted in an economically viable, environmentally responsible and ethical manner. This should include reducing investments in any companies linked to unethical or environmentally harmful practices, the switch to an environmentally ethical insurance provider, and the switch to an ethical banking provider. 2.1.3. Striving for sustainable food production, where food policy and procurement includes fair, ethical, and environmentally friendly items. This would include moving towards a more plant-based University, using the Green Shoots cafe as an example, and an even further reduction of single use plastics within the University, building on the work recognised in the University’s Green Grown Award 2024. 2.2. Ensuring all supply chains are fair, ethical, and environmentally sustainable. 2.2.1. Source only reused/recycled products where possible, such as paper, plastics, and other recyclables. 2.2.2. Publishing a detailed plan for working towards a zero-waste policy. 2.3. Ensuring services run by the University have been fully assessed for their environmental impact, including impact on overall carbon footprint, biodiversity and ecological resilience. 2.3.1. Ensuring transport services see a transition to electric vehicles. 2.3.2. Promoting the use of Active Travel across university campuses. 2.4. Net zero and environmental accountability. 2.4.1. Establish an Environmental Impact Committee, including Senior University Leadership, Students’ Union Representatives, and student groups to provide accountability for Net Zero promises, biodiversity targets and environmental sustainability targets. 3. The Sabbatical and Campaign Officers lobby the University and its staff, and campaign to encourage students to take action to reduce their own environmental impact and carbon footprint. Including, but not limited to, running campaigns around reducing waste, making more ethical choices for consumption, promoting active travel and use of public transport, promoting green jobs, eating more plant-based foods and promoting biodiversity. 4. The Sabbatical and Campaign Officers lobby the University its staff, and campaign to students to increase awareness of the climate, nature and biodiversity crises. Promoting individual and community action to curb these crises, encouraging all members of the University and Students’ Union community to be environmentally sustainable members of our global community. 5. The Sabbatical and Campaign Officers to work to develop an action plan for the Students' Union, similar to the University’s ‘Ecosystem Resilience and Biodiversity Action Plan 2024-2026’ and ‘Environmental Sustainability Plan 2025-2035'. The action plan would outline the SU’s commitment to environmental sustainability and biodiversity protection and improvements. This would include specific actionable targets and levels of accountability and be in line with the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals and the Well-Being of Future Generations Act Wales (2015). Cardiff SU Elected Officer Teams will re-evaluate where it engages with the police, and following this, continue to restrict engagement with the police to the minimum without violating legal requirements and interfering with strictly essential operations. Cardiff SU will work towards non-engagement with the police in the future. The immediate priorities in cutting down engagement with the police include refusing, opposing, and resisting police presence on campus, especially to promote career opportunities (including voluntary) and to promote themselves as the sole legitimate protectors of our safety. 3. Cardiff SU officers will also lobby Cardiff University to take the same stance and cut ties with the police as much as possible. They will also lobby the Halls of Residence to prevent police events taking place, as has been the case in the past. We understand this will not stop the police, with warrants, from investigating crime on Cardiff SU premises, nor from arriving in response to calls from individual students who choose to call the police and seek justice through this system. 4. Cardiff SU elected officer teams, especially its Advice service, will continue to support students who wish to pursue justice by reporting to and working with the police. 5. Cardiff SU elected officer teams will actively promote alternatives to policing and transformative justice practices, steering away from promoting the police and the carceral justice system as the only channel that survivors could pursue, while raising awareness of the police’s complicity in violence and sexual violence. Cardiff SU will broaden its definition of safety in its campaigns to acknowledge how policing perpetuates violence, and that students can feel unsafe around the police. 6. Cardiff SU elected officer teams will work with local and national organisations as well as student groups to raise awareness of police violence within our community, and to provide students with resources about resisting police violence, supporting victims of police brutality as a bystander, and knowing our rights when facing police violence. 7. Cardiff SU elected officer teams will publicly oppose and condemn the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022, especially its potential to suppress student protests, which are essential parts of students’ voice and democracy. In addition to this, elected officers should encourage amplification of student voices through protest or other indirect means on a rolling basis. 8. Cardiff SU elected officer teams will provide resources to facilitate transformative justice practices at Cardiff University as an alternative to policing in addressing student safety, focusing on education, bystander interventions, and community care. 9. Cardiff SU’s elected officers must lobby the university to allow students that have been arrested for protesting or related offences to remain on campus, and receive adequate support and contact for resources, mental health services and hardship funding. Passed by Senate 05/02/2026 Campaign for cut for university management and staff on £100,000 to £350,000 per year to save jobs and educational provision; and for replacing university management with an elected executive board Submitted by James Scott Motion Resolves: 1. The Sabbatical Officers publicly ask and lobby the university, and campaign to raise student and stakeholder support (e.g., through writing open letters, starting petitions, distributing educational materials etc.) for employees of the university who are in the full-time equivalent salary or wage bracket of over £100,000 per year taking pay and benefits cuts, as detailed below, each year until the motion expires in February 2029 or the desired outcomes are achieved: 1.1. Cutting the pay of each employee in the full-time equivalent salary or wage bracket between £100,000 and £150,000 by at least 15% from their nominal pay in financial year 2023-24, not including any employees that leave or are removed from their roles. 1.2. Cutting the pay of each employee in the full-time equivalent salary or wage bracket between £150,000 and £200,000 by at least 20% from their nominal pay in financial year 2023-24, not including any employees that leave or are removed from their roles. 1.3. Cutting the pay of each employee in the full-time equivalent salary or wage bracket over £200,000 by at least 25% from their nominal pay in financial year 2023-24, not including any employees that leave or are removed from their roles. 1.4. Removing all bonuses and benefits in kind for employees in the full-time equivalent salary bracket over £100,000 until the end of financial year 2028-29. 1.5. So that a pay scale is operated at the university where no one is renumerated at a rate of more than four times the median renumeration of all staff, where the median renumeration is calculated on a full-time equivalent basis for the salaries and wages paid by the institution. 1.6. So that a pay scale is operated at the university where no one is renumerated at a rate of more than ten times the full-time equivalent wage or salary of the staff on the lowest pay rate working at the institution. 1.7. Freezing nominal renumeration for those in the full-time equivalent salary or wage bracket over £100,000 after the changes in 1.1 to 1.6 are made, until the end of financial year 2028-29. 1.8. Reducing the total compensation to key management personnel by at least 20% from their nominal compensation in financial year 2023-24, and freezing the absolute total value of compensation for key management personnel until the end of financial year 2028-29. 2. In their campaigning and lobbying activities, the Sabbatical Officers should also be clear that: 2.1. These cuts should be reflected in the pay of new employees for the £100,000+ full-time equivalent salary or wage bracket. 2.2. The money saved should be used to reduce redundancies to staff, prevent jobs being downgraded and/or reduce cuts to schools of the university. 3. The Sabbatical Officers lobby the university, and campaign for student and stakeholder support (e.g., through writing open letters, starting petitions, distributing educational materials etc.) for all members of the university executive board to be elected democratically by students and staff. 4. The Students’ Union initiates a consultation with students, staff and trade union branches at Cardiff University and other relevant parties to draft a framework and guidelines for the electoral process required for democratically electing a university executive board. Passed by Senate 05/02/2026 Anti-Racism is a Verb: A Call for Racial Justice at Cardiff University Submitted by Faaiza Bashir Motion Resolves: 1. Commit to becoming an anti-racist organisation. 2. Developing an anti-racist action plan with measurable goals and accountability by 2027. 3. Run a rolling campaign of communication and education about anti-racism to SU staff and trustees, elected officers and the student body. 4. Embed anti-racist policy across the portfolio of work of the students union, not restricted to one voluntary campaign officer. Each elected officer should consider intersectionality and the experience of racialised students in their area of remit. 5. Campaign to hold the University to account to make the university policies, practices and services truly anti-racist, from policy to practice. All services should make the university an inclusive and place of belonging for all ethnic minority students. 6. Campaign the University to decolonise education by eradicating racism and colonialism, and elevate marginalised voices. 7. To work to implement all Students’ Union staff, trustees and elected officers annual anti-racism training, with additional training for Sabbatical and Elected Officers. Passed by Senate 05/12/2024 Defend and Extend Postgraduate Space on Campus Submitted by Micaela Panes Motion Resolves: 1. Cardiff Students' Union elected officers should actively lobby the university to reconsider the closure of the Postgraduate Study Zone, emphasising its significance to postgraduate students’ academic success, well-being, and sense of community. 2. Cardiff Students' Union elected officers should urge the university to seek alternative solutions that do not involve the loss of dedicated postgraduate study spaces. 3. Cardiff Students' Union elected officers should work with the university to find an alternative space for the Postgraduate Study Zone, which is 24/7, central, and meets all other postgraduate requirements. 4. Cardiff Students' Union elected officers should ensure that dedicated PGR offices are not implicated and remain dedicated to postgraduate research students only. Passed by Senate 05/12/2024 A Democratic University - Campaign for an Elected Chancellor Submitted by Jake Enea Motion Resolves: 1. To call for the establishment of a formal process for the election of a Chancellor at Cardiff University, ensuring the inclusion of all stakeholders in the university community. 2. To initiate a consultation with students, faculty, alumni, and other relevant parties to draft a framework and guidelines for the electoral process. 3. To advocate for the necessary changes to the university's statutes and regulations to facilitate the transition from appointment to election of the Chancellor. 4. To call on the Students' Union to actively campaign for this initiative, raising awareness among the student body and gathering support for the push towards a democratically elected Chancellor. Passed by Senate 06/02/2025 Cardiff Council all-Party Council Group for Students Submitted by Tomos Stokes Motion Resolves: 1. Resolves that the union should work to liaise with Cardiff Council using the APCG mechanism to assemble a group of pro-student councillors to stand up for the rights of students, advocating for policy passed by the SU and other policy deemed by the union to be to the benefit of students by acting as the group's secretariat, such as housing matters, student parking and waste collection. Passed by Senate 06/02/2025 Protect OUR Academic Future; Support Students and Staff Submitted by Micaela Panes Motion Resolves: 1. Cardiff Students’ Union Elected Officers will gather and encourage student questions, concerns, and feedback to ensure their voices are heard and represented at every level and every stage Cardiff Students’ Union Elected Officers will demand clear assurances that current students will not suffer as a result of these proposals. This includes clarity on course closures, school mergers, module availability, and student support services. 2. Cardiff Students’ Union Elected Officers will gather student questions, concerns, and feedback to ensure their voices are heard and represented at every level and every stage. 3. Cardiff Students’ Union Elected Officers will work alongside trade unions, affected schools, and key stakeholders to fight for alternative solutions; recognising the indispensable role of academic and professional service staff in student success. 4. In periods of industrial action, Cardiff Students’ Union Elected Officers will actively stand in solidarity with UCU (University College Union) to show recognition of the value university staff have in shaping students experiences and futures. This includes, but is not limited to, actively supporting staff at picket lines and expressing support. 5. Cardiff Students’ Union Elected Officers will continue to advocate for postgraduate research students ability to teach and will fight against any reduction in PGR teaching roles, recognising the importance of these roles in learning and development opportunities. Passed by Senate 06/02/2025 Ending Cardiff University’s Complicity with War and Violence Submitted by Daniel Green Motion Resolves: 1. To support students in feeling safe and welcome on campus by lobbying the university to end its complicity: a. To lobby the university to strengthen the ethical investment policy so that there is no investing in or partnering with companies that are complicit in human rights abuses as a matter of moral importance for the SU. This will demonstrate support of Cardiff students’ values and beliefs, since they have demonstrated that they are uncomfortable with the university’s complicity as it stands. b. To lobby the university to divest from companies, or funds which indirectly invest in those companies, which are complicit in human rights abuses in Palestine as a matter of moral importance for the SU. This will ensure that particularly those students who come from Palestine, and other affected countries, feel comfortable on campus and do not see their fees given to companies which act against their interests. c. To lobby the Student Futures team specifically, to review policies regarding: I. Allowing recruiters that profit from, or contribute to the violation of international law and Palestinian human rights, on campus. II. Vetting of jobs and companies advertised to students that contribute to and profit from the violation of international law and Palestinian human rights, to further improve student wellbeing, especially Middle Eastern students. This will ensure that all students feel able to attend events and are not prevented from accessing opportunities due to moral objections and/or traumatic associations with the companies present. d. To lobby the university to engage in good faith with students and student groups who wish to speak out over the complicity of the university in the outlined human rights abuses so that they are safeguarded better. Passed by Senate 06/02/2025 A Better Future for Welsh Students Submitted by Deio Owen Motion Resolves: 1. Cardiff Students’ Union believes in and supports Independence for Wales, for the advancement of education of students, through supporting a Wales void of Westminster rule and control, being able to create a better education system for Wales. 2. The Students’ Union should lobby the University to refuse to nominate individuals for National Honours that are connected to the British Empire. 3. The Union and its officers will not suggest names for the University to nominate for National Honours that are connected to the British Empire (by the discretion of the CUSU Board of Trustees) 4. The Union and its Officers shall lobby the University to use other national awards and honours rather than those connected to the British Empire. 5. The Union shall release a statement opposing National Honours that are connected with the British Empire as it goes against our values as an organisation. 6. By supporting an Independent Wales, the Union shall look at and campaign for new options for a national body to represent the students of Wales outside of NUS UK. 7. The Union and its officers shall demand that the University acknowledge and reject participating in Empirical systems. Passed by Senate 22/02/2024 Advocation for the Abolition of Tuition Fees Motion Resolves: 1. To support tuition fee abolition and forgiveness of student debt for all, international and national students; 2. To support and promote activist action on the subject of tuition fee abolition and forgiveness of student debt, while strongly encouraging Cardiff University societies to do the same. Passed by Senate 05/12/2023 Measuring Student Parent Intake Submitted by Zara Siddique Motion Resolves: 1. For the Students Union to consult with Cardiff University to begin measuring intake of student parents and to produce statistics around student parents and their learning experience. 2. To ensure there are ways for current students to declare parental responsibility after enrollment, i.e. if their circumstances change. 3. For the Students Union to ensure they will be able to reach out to students with parental responsibilities to make them aware of the services and support available to them. Passed by Senate 05/04/2023 Gender Identity Fund Submitted by Nodie Caple-Faye Motion Resolves: 1. For the Students’ Union to campaign for the introduction of a Gender Identity fund, funded by the University and administered by the Students’ Union. 2. For this fund to be designed to support students who wish to obtain the correct size of gender affirming items. 3. For the Students’ Union to promote the fund, once available, to the study body with particular focus on transgender and non-binary students. 4. For the fund to take account for the recommended application and awarding process as outlined in Appendix A. Passed by Senate 04/05/2023 Change the way we talk about ethnicity Submitted by Penny Dinh Motion Resolves: 1. Cardiff SU will permanently change the title of the role of Black and Ethnic Minority Officer to Anti-racism Officer, with “anti-racism” signifying Cardiff SU’s value and commitment to take actions against racism. 2. Cardiff SU will work with the current Black and Ethnic Minority Officer as well as future Anti-racism Officers to create a guidance on communicating about ethnicities and racism, which will be circulated to its staff members, trustees, as well as student societies and student leaders. This work will involve consultation with the student body and review of best practice adopted by other organisations, such as the UK and Welsh governments. 3. Cardiff SU officers will lobby Cardiff University to also adopt best practice in communicating about ethnicities and racism, steering away from the use of the BME and BAME umbrella terms, as well as the terminology of “political Blackness”. Passed by Senate 04/05/2023 Cardiff University Students' Union and Graduation 2023 Submitted by Micaela Panes Motion Resolves: 1. This motion resolves that Cardiff Students’ Union will not send Sabbatical Trustees, Campaigns Officers, or any representatives of past, present, or incoming to attend or represent the Students’ Union at Graduation 2023, in the case that UCU takes industrial action in the week of Graduation 2023. This includes making speeches at graduation ceremonies, attending Cardiff University graduation dinners, or related activities. 2. This motion resolves that Cardiff Students’ Union makes a public statement condemning Cardiff University’s choice to deduct 50-100% of pay from staff participating in the MAB, ASOS, or similar industrial action. Passed by Senate 19/06/2023 Carers Awareness Week Submitted by Nodie Caple-Faye Motion Resolves: 1. To have a Carer and parents awareness week during the first term (possibly after election week as it was in 2018), with a family day and /or a Give it a Go Trip. 2. To have those Sabbatical Officers dealing with Welfare involved with the lead being the Campaign officer and to involve the Together at Cardiff Officer. 3. To make this an annual event. Gall unrhyw fyfyriwr ym Mhrifysgol Caerdydd bleidleisio. How does the voting system work? Sut mae’r system bleidleisio’n gweithio? Voting in Students' Union election is one way you can ensure your voice is
                                        heard. Our elections use the single transferable voting method. Transferable
                                        voting allows voters to list the candidates in order of preference. The
                                        successful candidate will need 50% of the total number of votes plus 1 to win.
                                        If any candidate does not receive enough votes to win, the candidate with the
                                        fewest votes is removed and their votes transferred to the other candidates
                                        according to voters’ next preference. Mae pleidleisio yn etholiad Undeb y Myfyrwyr yn un ffordd y gallwch sicrhau bod eich llais yn cael ei glywed. Mae ein hetholiadau'n defnyddio'r dull pleidleisio trosglwyddadwy sengl. Mae pleidleisio trosglwyddadwy yn caniatáu i bleidleiswyr restru'r ymgeiswyr yn nhrefn eu dewis. Bydd angen 50% o gyfanswm y pleidleisiau ynghyd ag 1 ar yr ymgeisydd llwyddiannus i ennill. Os nad yw unrhyw ymgeisydd yn derbyn digon o bleidleisiau i ennill, caiff yr ymgeisydd gyda'r lleiaf o bleidleisiau ei dynnu a chaiff ei bleidleisiau eu trosglwyddo i'r ymgeiswyr eraill yn ôl dewis nesaf y pleidleiswyr. If you don't believe any of the candidates standing for a position have the

Start a Campaign. If you think something’s unfair, believe more awareness is needed around an issue, or want to change the way things are done – you can run a campaign. Campaigns can take many forms: Whether it’s writing an open letter, proposing a new policy through a motion, organising an event, or raising awareness on campus – there are plenty of ways to make your voice heard and create real change. Got an idea for a campaign? Get in touch with SUCampaigns@cardiff.ac.uk . The booklet which is available both on paper and online explains how to access modest healthcare dress. Behind the scenes, there has been lots of collaboration with both Cardiff University and the NHS to ensure appropriate infrastructure is in place so that students can access modest healthcare dress. We will continue to publicise this to students over the coming years to ensure students know they have the choice when it comes to healthcare dress code because it is your scrubs, you should have your choice." "Mae'r cynnig Fy Ngwisg, Fy Newis a gyflwynwyd yn y CCB ym mis Tachwedd 2025 wedi'i gwblhau'n swyddogol gyda phob penderfyniad wedi'i fodloni. Mae'r llyfryn, sydd ar gael ar bapur ac ar-lein, yn esbonio sut i gael mynediad at wisg gofal iechyd cymedrol. Y tu ôl i'r llenni, bu llawer o gydweithio â Phrifysgol Caerdydd a'r GIG i sicrhau bod seilwaith priodol ar waith fel y gall myfyrwyr gael mynediad at wisg gofal iechyd cymedrol. Byddwn yn parhau i gyhoeddi hyn i fyfyrwyr dros y blynyddoedd nesaf i sicrhau bod myfyrwyr yn gwybod bod ganddynt y dewis o ran cod gwisg gofal iechyd oherwydd mai eich gwisg chi yw hi, a dylech chi gael eich dewis." Josh Your VP Heath Park 2025-26 Eich Is-lywydd Parc y Mynydd Bychan 2025-26 (Published April 2026). (Cyhoeddwyd ym mis Ebrill 2026). "With the rise of racism across Wales in the last couple of years, including riots and protests against immigration, students of colour have felt isolated. We ran regular Emotional Support Groups throughout the year which has now been taken up by the University and made into the Athena Swan Focus Group, which aims to use student experiences on campus in their work towards equality at Cardiff University!" "Gyda chynnydd mewn hiliaeth ar draws Cymru yn ystod y blynyddoedd diwethaf, gan gynnwys terfysgoedd a phrotestiadau yn erbyn mewnfudo, mae myfyrwyr o liw wedi teimlo'n ynysig. Fe wnaethon ni gynnal Grwpiau Cymorth Emosiynol rheolaidd drwy gydol y flwyddyn sydd bellach wedi'u mabwysiadu gan y Brifysgol ac wedi'u troi'n Grŵp Ffocws Athena Swan, sy'n anelu at ddefnyddio profiadau myfyrwyr ar y campws yn eu gwaith tuag at gydraddoldeb ym Mhrifysgol Caerdydd!" Kavi Your Anti-Racism Officer 2025-26 Eich Swyddog Gwrth-Hiliaeth 2025-26 (Published March 2026). (Cyhoeddwyd ym mis Mawrth 2026). "Since the loss of the Postgraduate Study Zone post-Covid, there hasn’t been a dedicated, and central, space for our postgraduate students to carry out their studies or research. Consequently, I’ve been working closely with the University Library Team, and we are thrilled to announce that we’ve secured a dedicated postgraduate study space in the ASSL. This is the first step towards lobbying the University for a new postgraduate zone by showing them that there is a demand for such space. This is an exciting student win and a positive stepping stone for the future!" "Ers colli'r Parth Astudio Ôl-raddedig ar ôl Covid, nid oes lle canolog, penodol wedi bod i'n myfyrwyr ôl-raddedig i astudio neu gynnal eu hymchwil. O ganlyniad, rydw i wedi bod yn gweithio'n agos gyda Thîm Llyfrgell y Brifysgol, ac rydym yn falch iawn o gyhoeddi ein bod wedi sicrhau lle astudio yn benodol i ôl-raddedigion yn yr ASSL. Dyma'r cam cyntaf tuag at lobïo'r Brifysgol am barth ôl-raddedig newydd trwy ddangos iddynt fod galw clir am le o'r fath. Mae hon yn fuddugoliaeth gyffrous i fyfyrwyr ac yn gam cadarnhaol ymlaen ar gyfer y dyfodol!" Sean Your VP Postgraduate Students 2025-26 Eich Is-Ilwydd Myfyrwyr Ôl-raddedig 2025-26 (Published January 2025). (Cyhoeddwyd ym mis Ionawr 2025). "School HR did not process postgraduate tutor and demonstrator timesheets before the Christmas period and therefore SHARE PGRs would not have been paid for 2 months since carrying out employment. This delay would have had a serious impact on their financial stability. I raised this immediately with University HR and worked with them to ensure that our tutors and demonstrators got paid on time. The University HR team worked hard to process these timesheets, and therefore this issue was resolved and SHARE PGRs were paid at the end of January as per traditional timeframe." "Ni wnaeth Adnoddau Dynol yr Ysgol brosesu taflenni amser tiwtoriaid ac arddangoswyr ôl-raddedig cyn cyfnod y Nadolig ac felly ni fyddai myfyrwyr PGR SHARE yn cael eu talu am 2 fis ers cyflawni’r gwaith. Campus Welcome international students – this is your go-to source for the latest events, news and support services specific to the international community at Cardiff University. This page is designed to help you stay informed, get involved, and access the resources you need to make the most of your time here. Whether you are looking for updates on upcoming events, opportunities to connect with other students, or guidance and support during your student journey, you’ll find it here. Croeso fyfyrwyr rhyngwladol – dyma ble i ddod ar gyfer unrhyw ddigwyddiadau, newyddion, a chefnogaeth benodol ar gyfer cymuned ryngwladol Prifysgol Caerdydd. Mae’r dudalen hon wedi’i dylunio i'ch helpu i gymryd rhan a chael mynediad at yr adnoddau gallwch eu hangen tra byddwch yma. Boed os ydych yn edrych am ddiweddariadau ynghylch digwyddiadau, cyfleoedd i gysylltu gyda myfyrwyr eraill, neu arweiniad a chefnogaeth, dewch o hyd iddo yma. Hello everyone, welcome to Cardiff! I’m Hanan, your VP International for 2025/26. I’m here to represent you in matters of education and wellbeing and to ensure your experience at Cardiff University is as good as it can possibly be! Shwmae bawb, croeso i Gaerdydd! Ana ydw i, eich IL Rhyngwladol ar gyfer 2024/25. Rydw i yma i'ch cynrychioli mewn materion addysg a lles, ac i sicrhau bod eich profiad ym Mhrifysgol Caerdydd cystal ag y gall fod! Activities Cymdeithasau The Union’s societies and sports clubs are great opportunities to meet likeminded friends. Our societies range from interest based, to cultural, and academic. If you can think of it, there will probably be a society. We also have over 70 sports clubs one can join, with a lot of them competing in BUCS (British Universities and Colleges Sport) every Wednesday, and in Welsh Varsity (against Swansea University) every Spring. Mae dros 200 o gymdeithasau i gymryd rhan ynddynt, dim ots beth rydych chi'n ei astudio. Peidiwch fod ofn ymuno yn yr hwyl! Mae ymuno â chymdeithasau yn ffordd wych o wneud ffrindiau, dysgu pethau newydd, a gwella eich CV a sgiliau cyflogadwyedd. Join a Society Join a Sports Club Student Advice Cyngor i Fyfyrwyr Housing Are you having issues with your accommodation? Is your landlord making you feel uncomfortable? Are you unsure about signing your new housing contract? The Students’ Union’s Advice service can answer all your questions and give you free, confidential advice on matters regarding housing . Academic Appeals Are you going through an academic appeal procedure or would like to start one? Our Advice team can help you with this. Issues we can’t help you with Visa enquiries : We are not legally allowed to provide any Visa advice, but you can contact the Student Connect team at the University or use the information on their website . Llety Yn cael trafferth gyda llety? Landlord newydd yn eich gwneud i deimlo’n anghyfforddus? Yn ansicr am arwyddo cytundeb? Gall gwasanaeth cyngor Undeb Myfyrwyr Caerdydd ateb eich holl gwestiynau a darparu cyngor cyfrinachol am ddim ar faterion llety . Apelio academaidd Ydych chi’n mynd trwy’r weithdrefn apelio academaidd neu eisiau dechrau apêl? Gall ein tîm cynghori eich helpu gyda hyn. Materion penodol ni allwn helpu gyda Ymholiadau fisa :Yn gyfreithiol, nid oes hawl gennym ddarparu unrhyw gyngor fisa, ond gallwch gysylltu â thîm Cyswllt Myfyrwyr y Brifysgol neu ddefnyddio’r wybodaeth ar eu gwefan . You can contact our Advice team via email , or by calling 02920 781410 (active Mon-Fri 9am-5pm). Gallwch gysylltu gydag ein tîm cyngor dros e-bost neu trwy ffonio 02920 781410 (dydd Llun-Gwener 9yb-5yh). Student Voice Llais y Myfyrwyr At the Students’ Union, we want to empower you to use your voice to improve your experience at Cardiff University. Yn Undeb y Myfyrwyr rydym am roi’r grym i chi i ddefnyddio eich lleisiau i wella eich profiad ym Mhrifysgol Caerdydd. Student Academic Representatives Every cohort has at least one Student Academic Rep who collects feedback and attends the Student Staff Panels (SSP) where they provide feedback to the university staff. Vice President of International Students (Sabbatical Officer) The VP International ensures that the rights and wellbeing of international students are not compromised in the University’s projects. You could be the next VP International; you just need to nominate yourself in the next Spring Elections and get elected! International Executive Committee This group is made of 12 engaged international students who meet fortnightly with the VP International and relay feedback gathered from their peers on what students want to see. They volunteer their time for the International Network events, which is essential for these events to take place. They’ll also hold the VP International to account and ensure their working reflects what students want to see. Cynrychiolwyr Academaidd Myfyrwyr Mae gan bob carfan neu gwrs o leiaf un Cynrychiolydd Academaidd sy’n casglu adborth a’n mynychu Paneli Staff-Myfyrwyr, lle maent yn darparu adborth i staff y Brifysgol (academyddion, llyfrgellwyr, arlwyo...). Is-lywydd Myfyrwyr Rhyngwladol (Swyddog Sabothol) Dyma’r flwyddyn gyntaf i fyfyriwr cael eu hethol fel IL Myfyrwyr Rhyngwladol amser llawn! Mae’r IL Rhyngwladol yn sicrhau yn amddiffyn hawliau a lles myfyrwyr rhyngwladol yn y Brifysgol. Gallech chi fod yr IL Rhyngwladol nesaf; enwebwch eich hun yn Etholiadau’r Gwanwyn i gael eich ethol! Pwyllgor Gweithredol Rhyngwladol Mae’r grŵp hwn yn cynnwys 12 myfyriwr rhyngwladol sy’n cwrdd gyda’r IL Rhyngwladol bob pythefnos i ddarparu adborth gan eu cyd-fyfyrwyr am yr hyn hoffent ei weld yn digwydd. Maent yn gwirfoddoli eu hamser yn nigwyddiadau’r Rhwydwaith Rhyngwladol, sy’n hanfodol er mwyn cynnal y digwyddiadau yma. Maent hefyd yn cadw’r IL Rhyngwladol yn atebol a’n sicrhau bod eu gwaith yn adlewyrchu’r hyn y mae myfyrwyr am ei weld. Check out the Student Voice webpages to learn more about Elections, Student Senate, Speak Week and the Annual General Meeting (AGM). All students are invited to attend the AGM and cast their vote on the proposals that will affect their student experience. Ewch draw i dudalen Llais y Myfyrwyr i ddysgu mwy am Etholiadau, Senedd y Myfyrwyr, Wythnos Siarad, a’r Cyfarfod Cyffredinol Blynyddol (CCB). Gwahoddir pob myfyriwr i'r CCB i bleidleisio ar gynigion a fydd yn effeithio ar eu profiadau fel myfyrwyr. should every international student know once they arrive in Cardiff? This page provides information to help you settle into your new home in Wales. Housing As you move out into private housing, it’s important that you do your due diligence. When it comes to your landlord, you should check if they are registered with Rent Smart Wales . This will let you know whether the landlord has a licence to let the property out, any agents associated with the property, if the property has an Energy Performance Certificate , and more. Knowing this information beforehand can prevent any problems happening later down the line! We also have our Housing Help campaign page , which can give you guidance if you do end up having issues in your house. We have email templates for multiple different situations, so you can professionally correspond with your landlord on a range of issues. During your time at university, you may need academic help and support as an international student. This page provides information and ways to get help with your studies. Student Mentor Scheme Joining the Student Mentor Scheme in your course is a great way to learn the ins and outs of being a Cardiff University student. You will be assigned a senior student in your course who will arrange meetings with you to discuss the course, accommodations, and the general student life. It could be a great opportunity to enhance your student journey. Student Reps Student Reps serve as the link between the student body and teaching staff. They bring their peer’s feedback to staff within the academic schools to help develop and improve your course. There is a student representative for every year in every course, including Master’s and Postgraduate Research. If you have feedback for your course, get in touch with your student rep!
