Union President: Georgia Spry It has been an absolute pleasure being your Vice President Sports and Athletic Union President for the past 2 years. There have been many challenging times but I’m so proud of the Sabbatical Officer team for their unwavering support for students and consistently challenging the University to do better. Some of my largest highlights this year were Welsh Varsity, SU Fight Night, my amazing AU Executive Committee and increasing the visibility of Sports Clubs on social media. This year I have: Launched the Let’s Talk Consent campaign educating students on Sexual Violence and how to be an active bystander. Produced weekly Sport Spotlights highlighting our amazing Sports Clubs and their achievements to give them more visibility and exposure on the AU and SU social media pages. Promoted inclusivity in sports during LGBTQ+ History Month by challenging clubs to wear their rainbow laces and ribbons to training and games and challenge inappropriate language. Celebrated our clubs be reintroducing Team of the Week and Club of the Month. Launched the Fixtures and Results webpage to promote our Club’s competition achievements throughout the year. Organized one of the largest student sporting events in the UK – Welsh Varsity, with 10,000 spectators and 1000 athletes. Ran the SU Fight Night with Kickboxing, MMA and Taekwondo growing on last year’s success with all the profits going to the Sports Clubs involved. Represented Welsh sport, universities and student unions as the Student Chair of Welsh Student Sports and sat on the BUCS Advisory Panel as the Welsh student representative. Continued the AU referral scheme to the hardship fund run by the Financial Assistance Programme in the University. I attended Club Give it a Go’s at the start of the year and created social media content to promote non-BUCS and less known sports. Restructured our committee training to make it more engaging by introducing interactive elements, new slide designs, new timetable and alternating staff delivery as well as introducing topics on bystander training and culture change. Diolch for voting me in twice, it’s been an intense but rewarding two years and I hope I have left a better Students’ Union than I came into. Officer Team 2023-2024 VP Undergraduate Students (Education and Welfare): Noah Russell I’ve loved my second year in this role, working with the team has been an absolute joy and so much has been achieved. It’s definitely not been an easy year, but I am so incredibly proud of the team for persevering and making a difference to the lives of Cardiff Students. In my second and final year as a sabbatical officer I have completed much of what I was hoping for during my time here, but there is always more to do which I am excited to see from our new sabbatical officer team of 2024/25. This year I have: Supported students in getting compensation after being affected by the strikes and Marking and Assessment Boycott. Secured free drug testing kits for all students, so that if students do decide to take substances they can know what they are taking and if it is safe. Helped create a new Gender Identity Fund, allowing trans and non-binary students access to gender affirming products and care. This is the first of its kind at Cardiff University and we cannot wait to see it being used by our queer students. Proudly called for a ceasefire in Gaza and stood with our students in supporting the victims of the genocide in Palestine. Helped implement the findings from our Cops Off Campus Task and Finish group, ensuring the student voice was heard and listened to. Monitored and supported the implementation of Blackboard Ultra, meaning the digital learning environment of students should be more streamlined than ever. This has been a very successful project and has been completed throughout with student consultation, a brilliant example of how these projects should be done. Pushed for a greener Cardiff University, both metaphorically and literally. This has included looking into securing bee-houses on the SU roof, pushing the Fossil Free Careers motion forward and working with the university and local community on how we can make the local environment more accessible and pleasant to our students. Helped revalidate dozens of programs, ensuring that when programs and modules are proposed they are fully considered with student interests in mind. Represented the interests of students across committees and working groups from the senior management level of the university, to ground floor projects. Diolch for voting me in twice, it’s been an intense but rewarding two years and I hope I have left a better Students’ Union than I came into. VP Sports and Athletic Union President: Georgia Spry What a year! It has been an absolute pleasure being your Vice President Sports and Athletic Union President this year and I can’t wait to continue working with you all next year. My year has been full to the brim with projects, campaigns, sports and supporting our students. Some of my largest highlights were Welsh Varsity, bringing home the shield for the 26th Anniversary, pushing for more inclusivity and diversity, not only in sports but across the university, and running the first ever SU Fight Night with 2 styles of martial arts. I have enjoyed every second of it and look forward to continuing to champion our students’ voices and making sports bigger and better at Cardiff University. Here’s a taste of the projects I have worked on this year: I ran a DisAbility Sports campaign where we ran 3 para-sport events and released a podcast to raise awareness of disabilities in sports. Sober Socials Week highlighted the importance of clubs and societies hosting socials accessible to all members. I ran a Winter Wellbeing Campaign to tackle the winter blues. We hosted events, signposted, gave away wellbeing essentials and recorded a wholesome podcast on our experiences with winter blues and exam stress. Promoted inclusivity in sports during LGBTQ+ History Month by challenging clubs to wear their rainbow laces and ribbons to training and games. Organized one of the largest student sporting events in the UK – Welsh Varsity, with over 9000 spectators and 1000 athletes. Lead Team Cardiff to another huge Welsh Varsity win over Swansea (33.5 – 13.5!) Represented Welsh sport, universities and student unions as the Student Co-Chair of Welsh Student Sports and sat on the BUCS Advisory Panel as the  Welsh student representative. Improved communication between the AU and its members through monthly newsletters, social media and regular emails. Met with Club presidents twice a year to set goals as well as offering regular committee drop ins and meetings. Continued the AU referral scheme to the hardship fund run by the Financial Assistance Programme in the University. Recorded many podcasts covering a wide range of topics that link to the SU’s many campaigns (you can listen here !) Introduced Disability awareness training and Bystander Training as well as pushing for Wellbeing Training for the University Sport’s IMG teams. I updated the Tier System to include realistic requirements and reduce the jump between tiers. The new system requires an increase in Club effort as the tiers go up and consider the size of a club. Successfully ran the Students’ Union’s first ever Fight Night with Kickboxing and MMA. I attended Club Give it a Go’s at the start of the year and created social media content to promote non-BUCS and less known sports. Facilitated record numbers of students at our freshers fairs. VP Postgraduate Students (Education and Welfare): Micaela Panes I’ve had a busy year as your VP Postgraduate! I’ve loved representing and advocating for students this year and can’t wait to continue next year. Here’s a list of just some of what I’ve worked on and my student wins in my first year: This year I have: Ensured students who had their studies impacted by industrial action received compensation. Ensured that Graduate Tutor and Demonstrator contracts were implemented in all schools and chased down those who did not comply. Run a ‘PGRs: Know your Rights’ campaign to ensure that all Postgraduate Researchers were aware of their new rights under the new teaching contracts. Lobbied against the Welsh Government’s decision to axe Postgraduate grants and got over 2,000 signatures on the petition in a month. The petition was discussed by the Senedd’s Petitions Committee which made the Education Minister conduct and publish an equality impact assessment. Brought back ‘Postgraduate Welcome Fortnight’ and ran two weeks of sold-out events. Created the first ever ‘Research Aid’ boxes for Postgraduate Research students. Increased the library loan limit from 35 to 50 for all students and staff. Increased the Postgraduate Study Zone opening times to 24/7. Run 5 Postgraduate Exclusive Give it a Go trips to Oxford, Stonehenge and Salisbury, Bath, Rhossili, and Tenby – for only £5 (with HEFCW funding)! Grew the Postgraduate Association’s reputation and began rebuilding a strong Postgraduate community. Ran the first ever ‘Postgraduate Big Unwind’ to help students de-stress and meet new people. Created a ‘wellbeing area’ in the Postgraduate Study Zone with board games and colouring books. Began work on creating a cross-University PGR mentoring scheme. Wrote the first-ever Student View on the PGR Student Experience which covered teaching and demonstrating, community and belonging, funding and financial struggle, academic and student support, and supervision. Led a register to vote campaign in the lead up the 2024 General Election. Supported the University in reviewing the PGR Extenuating Circumstances and Interruption of Studies policies which now include huge wins for PGRs, such as simpler and a more accessible process, phased returns, working at limited capacity, and great support on return to study. Officer Team 2022-2023 SU President: Gina Dunn I have absolutely loved my second year as a sabbatical officer, stepping up to the role of President. This has been an extremely challenging year to be a student, with the Cost-of-Living Crisis and Industrial Action having a big impact on University life, but it has also been a fantastic one. The officer team have worked tirelessly to ensure students are represented in every decision made by both the University and the Union. Some of the things I’ve been working on includes: Getting the first ever VK Vending Machine. Increased the capacity of our club nights by opening the Balconi bar. Supported students through the Cost-of-Living Crisis by introducing £2 lunches, Feed Your Flat: The Essentials, free tea and coffee in the lounge and free breakfasts during exam times. Interviewed and appointed the new Vice Chancellor of the University. Reverted the Cardiff University Bursary to be available in cash. Reverted the Cardiff University Bursary to be available in cash. Ran Revision Aid in both exam periods with the entire team, introducing free breakfasts and printing in both the Cathays and Heath Park Campus. Booked in Blood Drives in the SU for November 2023. Ensured mitigation for exam boards during the Marking and Assessment boycott. Worked closely with the Welsh Language Officer to ensure a smooth transition to the new full time Vice President role. VP Sports and AU 
President: Olivia Evans It has been an absolute pleasure being the Vice President Sports & Athletic Union President this year. It has been a year of unbelievable moments and memories. Being able to be a big part of organizing and running the first home Varsity since pre-pandemic, in which we achieved the biggest win for team Cardiff ever recorded, has been the resounding highlight. However, the diversity work I have done this year has also been central to my experience. This year I strove to make sports as accessible to everyone as possible through disability sports initiatives as well as an extensive rainbow laces campaign. I hope that I will leave the sports landscape at Cardiff a more inclusive and safe space than it was when I arrived. Here is a taste of what I achieved as VP Sports & AU President: Ran two rainbow laces days – getting over 1200 athletes wearing them in solidarity with the LGBTQ+ community. Produced a large rainbow laces video campaign, giving voice to some of our LGBTQ+ athletes. Organized one of the largest student sporting events in the UK – over 8000 student spectators and over 800 competing athletes. Lead Team Cardiff to a record Varsity win over Swansea. Organized an awards ceremony for the Athletic Union, hosting 500 attendees.
Worked to develop disability sports at Cardiff. I represented Welsh sport in the BUCS community by sitting as the Student Chair for Welsh Student Sport as well as, as the Welsh representative on the BUCS Advisory Panel. I was a panel member on BUCS Disciplinary Panels. Spoke live on BBC Wales about Welsh Varsity. Organised a plethora of guest speakers on diversity and inclusion. Improved communication from the AU to its members through social media and newsletters. Improved the training of new committee members by returning training to in person, meeting with presidents twice in the year, and starting committee coffee mornings. Set up the first Athletic Union Hardship fund to support students through the cost-of-living crisis. Provided first aid kits to all BUCS playing teams. Improved conduct and behavior by introducing a new code of conduct and new training for clubs in conjunction with the university. Ran a successful Spring in Your Step Campaign accessible to both Cathays and the Heath. Ran a successful Nighttime safety campaign to signpost students to safety initiatives at the start of the year. VP Societies and Volunteering: Shreshth Goel It has been such a wonderful year for Societies and Volunteering this year. I have thoroughly enjoyed my time as VP Societies and Volunteering and am extremely proud of everything our student groups have achieved this year. From marking Gair Rhydd’s 50th anniversary to celebrating student accomplishments at National Societies and Volunteering Awards, we have done it all!  
Whilst the year did not come without its challenges, we have managed to grow the Guild membership and have welcomed new societies to the guild! Raising 1000s of pounds for various charities, our students have shown real dedication and commitment to Raise and Give this year and I am looking forward to seeing what’s next for them all. I would not have been able to do any of this without help from my team so a special shoutout to Ellen O’Dwyer, Hannah Snape, Sophie Irving, Rhys White, Paul Jones, and Rachel Mattey. This year we have started some exciting new things and I really hope they act as building blocks for what’s to come and these are events and campaigns that can grow even bigger and better in the future! Some of the things I’ve been working on includes: PrEPare Campaign where I promoted the use of PrEP, encouraged sexual health testing among students and even brought a variety of free contraceptives to the SU. I worked with the International Students Officer to organize and host ‘Culture Cwtch’, a celebration of Diversity. This event was a massive success and we managed to sell out with having to introduce extra standing tickets on the door! Introducing more mirrored spaces in the Union for our student groups.  
Securing more University rooms and buildings for student groups. Restructured the tier system – For the first time, this was passed by Societies Forum after a year of development and consultation with students. Pronoun Badge Distribution campaign where I gave out 100s of pronoun badges to students to create a more welcoming and inclusive environment around campus. Presidential Meetings where I held myself accountable by receiving feedback from individual society presidents by hosting 1-2-1s and working on their reviews. Lowering the Guild Costs for Erasmus Students. Promoted Volunteering by hosting a Volunteering Fair and working alongside the Volunteering Executive Committee on Student Volunteering Week. LGBTQ+ History Month where I hosted a range of events throughout February to promote LGBTQ+ history and support the community. Getting the first ever Drag Queen DJ in the SU for Pride YOLO in February. Opening the first ever eSports Suite in a Welsh Students’ Union. Introducing Taf Sunday Carvery Loyalty Cards for students during National Student Money Week. Improving Societies Committee Resources by writing a new Committee Handbook and Redesigning the Societies Website. Executive Committee Q&As Executive Committee Q&As Any tips for presentation assessments? Book a study-space room in Cochrane building with a screen and practise your presentation there. You can see how your slides look on a larger display, which helps reduce anxiety and allows you to check for any layout or formatting issues before the actual assessment. Also gets you used to presenting in the space. What can I do on campus if I have a long break between lectures? If it's a sunny day you can go to the heath park behind the hospital. They have a park and a little cafe. If it more of a rainy day, the IV lounge has games you can play. Also there is a Weatherspoon's you can go for an affordable lunch, a 20 minute walk away. Great for a refillable coffee if you are studying. What are the spaces available for studying and chilling in Heath Park? Heath Park Library (Cochrane Building): Main dedicated study space on Heath Park campus. Designed for medical and healthcare students but open to others too. Provides quiet zones for focused work and collaborative study areas with relevant books and resources. Open 24/7 for students. Students Union on Heath Park: There is a Students’ Union spot on the campus (The IV Lounge and IV Common Area in the Neuadd Meirionnydd building). These spaces are useful for socialising, meeting friends, and informal chill time between study sessions. While most formal cafe/social spaces are on the main Cathays campus, the on-site Students’ Union facilities may have informal seating and refreshments. Specialist Study Areas and IT Rooms: Each school/faculty building on Heath Park (like dentistry, medicine, and healthcare) has its own study spaces and IT facilities. These are available round-the-clock and good for individual work or group study. Lecture theatres and seminar rooms may sometimes be used for group study or activities outside teaching hours. Outdoor Parkland: Green Spaces Heath Park campus sits next to 100+ acres of parkland and playing fields, useful for breaks, relaxing, outdoor reading, or group chats when the weather’s nice. Sports & Leisure Facilities: The campus has sports amenities (pool, squash, badminton, gym) — great for unwinding and taking study breaks. What do I do if I want to prepare a hot meal on campus? Bringing food from home is a great way to save money, so we have a range of facilities available for you to use. The Cochrane Building: You'll find a hot water tap (perfect for instant noodles) and two microwaves (ideal for soups, meal prep, or last night's leftovers). The Common Room (opposite the IV Lounge): A student kettle and microwave are available here. How can I prepare for my first day on placement at the Heath? Your first day can feel a little nerve wracking, but a bit of preparation can go a long way! Here are 10 steps to help you feel confident and ready: Iron your scrubs or uniform the night before. It’s one less thing to worry about and helps you feel prepared. Gather your equipment (stethoscope, notebook, pen, pocket watch, ID badge, etc.) so you don’t have to scramble in the morning. Familiarise yourself with the site. The Heath can be easy to get lost in, so if possible, visit a few days before to find the wards, entrances, and locker rooms. Meal prep and pack snacks. Breaks can be short, and food options may be limited. Bring a refillable water bottle to stay hydrated throughout the day. Email your team or ward ahead of time to introduce yourself and check start times and expectations. Break down your sign-offs or competencies into smaller goals. Tackling them gradually can make them more manageable and give you a sense of achievement. Do some light pre-reading to familiarise yourself with the content and make learning easier. Plan to arrive a little early and make sure to introduce yourself every time even if it feels repetitive. Be kind to yourself. Ask questions, stay calm, and remember it’s completely normal to make mistakes. Make sure to treat yourself to something small after your first day, you’ve earned it :) Heath Park Campus Services Gwasanaethau Parc y Mynydd Bychan Our Student Advice team located in the Cathays Students' Union building provide academic, consumer, housing, advocacy and representation advice and support through a free, confidential, impartial and independent service to all members of the Students' Union. at first. We've put together some quick information to help you while you're away, and to remind you that the Students' Union is still here for you, even if you're not in Cardiff. Gall fynd ar leoliad fod yn un o brofiadau gorau eich bywyd ond gall y syniad godi ofn arnoch i ddechrau sy’n gwbl ddealladwy. Rydym wedi rhoi rhywfaint o wybodaeth at ei gilydd yn gyflym i’ch helpu tra byddwch i ffwrdd, ac i’ch atgoffa bod Undeb y Myfyrwyr dal yma i chi, hyd yn oed os nad ydych chi yng Nghaerdydd. We offer a series of activities where you are while you’re on placement. The activities are free and give you the chance to meet up with other students. Mae Parc y Mynydd Bychan ar Daith yn brosiect a ddechreuon ni i’ch cefnogi yn ystod eich profiad ar leoliad i ffwrdd o Gaerdydd. Rydym yn cynnig cyfres o weithgareddau lle rydych chi tra byddwch chi ar leoliad. Mae’r gweithgareddau am ddim ac yn rhoi cyfle i chi gwrdd â myfyrwyr eraill. Keep an eye on the upcoming events below to find out more information about Heath Park on Tour dates. Cadwch lygad ar y digwyddiadau sydd i ddod isod i gael rhagor o wybodaeth am ddyddiadau Parc y Mynydd Bychan ar Daith. That is what the My Scrubs, My Scrubs AGM motion was all about. We are pleased to share that we have completed the motion's resolves in full! Mae pob myfyriwr yn haeddu gallu gwisgo'n gymedrol am unrhyw reswm ar unrhyw adeg, gan gynnwys cod gwisg gofal iechyd. Dyna oedd bwriad cynnig CCB Fy Ngwisg, Fy Newis. Joshua, your VP Heath Park Campus, and Hanan, your VP International Students, have put together a handy information booklet titled, Your Scrubs, Your Choice, that details all the relevant information on how to access modest scrubs and what to do if you can't. Mae Joshua, eich IL Campws Parc y Mynydd Bychan, a Hanan, eich IL Myfyrwyr Rhyngwladol, wedi rhoi llyfryn gwybodaeth defnyddiol o'r enw, Eich Gwisg, Eich Dewis, at ei gilydd sy'n cynnwys yr holl wybodaeth berthnasol ar sut i gael mynediad at sgrubiau cymedrol a beth i'w wneud os na allwch chi. At the end of the booklet you will find a list of contact information should you have any questions regarding modesty requirements. Please do not hesitate to get in touch with your queries! Ar ddiwedd y llyfryn fe welwch restr o wybodaeth gyswllt os oes gennych unrhyw gwestiynau ynghylch gofynion cymedrol. Mae croeso i chi gysylltu â ni gydag unrhyw ymholiadau! Tackling Sexual Violence Mynd i'r Afael â Thrais Rhywiol Time to act: Mae’n Amser Gweithredu: Sexual violence and misconduct can happen anywhere, even on your placement. For students at Heath Park, this can be perpetuated by staff, patients or even your fellow students. With the healthcare setting being so fast paced it can be hard to know where to report or how to challenge such behaviour. Gall trais rhywiol a chamymddwyn ddigwydd yn unrhyw le, hyd yn oed ar leoliad. I fyfyrwyr ym Mharc y Mynydd Bychan, gall hyn ddigwydd gyda staff, cleifion neu hyd yn oed eich cyd-fyfyrwyr. Gyda'r maes gofal iechyd mor gyflym ei natur, gall fod yn anodd gwybod ble i roi gwybod amdano neu sut i herio ymddygiad o'r fath. BMA conducted a study with medical students which found that 41% of female and 19% of male respondents have experienced sexual assault during their studies, including on their clinical placement with 67% of those choosing not to report over fear that nothing would be done. Cynhaliodd BMA astudiaeth gyda myfyrwyr meddygol a ganfu fod 41% o fenywod a 19% o ddynion a ymatebodd wedi profi ymosodiad rhywiol yn ystod eu hastudiaethau, gan gynnwys ar eu lleoliad clinigol, gyda 67% o'r rhai yn dewis peidio ag adrodd oherwydd ofn na fyddai dim yn cael ei wneud. This shows just how systemic sexual misconduct is but just know you are not alone and this page is here to give you all the information you need. Mae hyn yn dangos pa mor systemig yw camymddwyn rhywiol, ond cofiwch nad ydych chi ar eich pen eich hun ac mae'r dudalen hon yma i roi'r holl wybodaeth sydd ei hangen arnoch chi. Whether something has happened to you on placement, in the past or is currently ongoing, or even if you are worried about someone else and how best to support them. This page will break down how and who you can report to and the support available to you as a student. P'un a yw rhywbeth wedi digwydd i chi ar leoliad, yn y gorffennol neu ar hyn o bryd, neu hyd yn oed os ydych chi'n poeni am rywun arall a'r ffordd orau o'u cefnogi. Bydd y dudalen hon yn esbonio sut a phwy allwch chi roi gwybod iddo a'r gefnogaeth sydd ar gael i chi fel myfyriwr. Whatever you choose to do and whenever you choose to do it, support is available to you. You deserve safety, dignity and love. Whatever has happened is not your fault and there are people available to you to speak to, no matter what, with no judgement . You do not have to do this alone; there is help available to you. Beth bynnag a ddewiswch ei wneud a phryd bynnag y dewiswch ei wneud, mae cefnogaeth ar gael i chi. Rydych chi'n haeddu diogelwch, urddas a chariad. Nid eich bai chi yw beth bynnag sydd wedi digwydd ac mae pobl ar gael i chi siarad â nhw, beth bynnag fo’r amgylchiadau, heb unrhyw farn. Nid oes rhaid i chi fynd trwy hyn ar eich pen eich hun; mae cymorth ar gael i chi. Depending on your circumstances you will need to choose the appropriate type of report, see below: Yn dibynnu ar eich amgylchiadau, bydd angen i chi ddewis y math priodol o adroddiad, gweler isod: Reporting University Staff Adrodd ar Staff y Brifysgol For reporting university staff use the Student Complaints Procedure . I adrodd ar staff y brifysgol, defnyddiwch y Weithdrefn Gwyno Myfyrwyr . Reporting Students Adrodd ar Fyfyrwyr For reporting students use the Student Conduct Procedure . I adrodd ar fyfyrwyr, defnyddiwch y Weithdrefn Gwyno Myfyrwyr . Reporting NHS Staff, Patients or the Public Adrodd ar Staff y GIG, Cleifion neu'r Cyhoedd For reporting NHS Staff, patients or the general public whilst on placement you should contact your personal tutor or your Placement Education Facilitator. In Addition you should also contact your respective NHS Health Board . I adrodd ar Staff y GIG, cleifion neu'r cyhoedd yn gyffredinol tra ar leoliad, dylech gysylltu â'ch tiwtor personol neu'ch Hwylusydd Addysg Lleoliadau. Yn ogystal, dylech hefyd gysylltu â'ch Bwrdd Iechyd GIG priodol. Report + Support Adrodd + Chymorth Report + Support is Cardiff University’s confidential tool for raising concerns and accessing support. This is not a formal reporting tool but it can start the process of giving you guidance and support in then being able to make the decision to formally report using one of the other methods above. Mae Adrodd + Cymorth yn offeryn cyfrinachol ym Mhrifysgol Caerdydd ar gyfer codi pryderon a chael mynediad at gymorth. Nid offeryn adrodd ffurfiol yw hwn ond gall ddechrau'r broses o roi arweiniad a chymorth i chi er mwyn gallu gwneud y penderfyniad i adrodd yn ffurfiol gan ddefnyddio un o'r dulliau eraill uchod. third floor of the Students' Union, Julian oversees SU Transport, providing a range of vehicles, including minibuses and large MPVs, to students and staff. The Transport Office not only offers access to vehicles but also conducts driver training and assessments to ensure safe driving practices. Operating from 9 am to 4 pm, the Transport desk is available for inquiries, though scheduling meetings is recommended through calls or emails due to ongoing testing and vehicle checks. Presently, we lease vehicles that clubs and societies can utilize for official trips. The current fleet includes 6 x 9-seater Ford Tourneo and 2 x 17 seater Ford Transit Mini Buses. Vehicle hires are possible with over 72 hours' notice, ranging from cars, SUVs, and MPVs to vans (both SWB and LWB) and minibuses. Note that driving a hired external 17-seater minibus requires a D1 endorsement on your license. In cases where all SU vehicles are allocated, clubs, societies, and other entities may still access vehicles at the full cost. Individuals eligible to drive these vehicles must pass a MiDAS test, with specific tests for different vehicle classes. For test details and registration, please visit the Student Portal. Contacting the Transport Department is easy. Reach out using the information below, and we'll strive to respond within 48 hours: SUTransport@cardiff.ac.uk Trafnidiaeth Ar drydydd llawr Undeb y Myfyrwyr, Julian yw ein goruchwyliwr trafnidiaeth gyda chyfrifoldeb am ddarparu amrywiaeth o gerbyd, gan gynnwys bysiau mini a faniau, i fyfyrwyr a staff. Mae'r adran drafnidiaeth ar agor o 9yb i 4yh ar gyfer ymholiadau, er rydym yn argymell trefnu cyfarfod er mwyn sicrhau ein bod ar gael am drafodaeth gyda chi. Ar hyn o bryd, rydym yn benthyg cerbydau i glybiau a chymdeithasau ar gyfer teithiau swyddogol. Mae ein cerbydau presennol yn cynnwys 6 x Ford Tourneo gyda 9 sedd a 2 x 17 Peugeot Bws. Mae modd llogi cerbydau gyda dros 72 awr o rhybudd, o geir i SUVs, a MPVs i faniau (SWB a LWB) a bysiau mini. Staff Employers Training Opportunities The Students’ Union offers training courses that provide you with the opportunity to develop your skills. By attending our courses, you will improve your employability and gain certification in key areas that are valued by future employers. Book a course Courses are available to Cardiff University students - to make a booking, login to the website. Professional Development in Leadership This diploma provides you with the opportunity to develop and enhance your leadership and interpersonal skills, as well as developing your knowledge of how to co-ordinate, motivate and shape individuals and team members. During this diploma you will attend workshops and evidence interpersonal experiences that you have undertaken in a work or voluntary situation. Please note, the Diploma Award has now been closed off to new applications. How do I complete the diploma? Attend 5 x 2 hour leadership workshops Record interpersonal experiences against laid down standards. These will be graded as follows: Gold: 3 separate records Silver: 2 separate records Bronze: 1 separate records Complete a Reflection & Articulation activity How much does the course cost? Free How will I receive my diploma? Once you complete the Diploma you will receive certification signed by Cardiff University's Vice Chancellor and the Students' Union President. An added bonus is that for $60.00 plus VAT you will be to receive an Institute of Leadership & Management additional accreditation. Contact us Emergency 1st Aid This course will provide you with basic training in Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and several additional emergencies and ailments. The course is recognised for 3 years. How do I complete the course? You will attend 1 x 6-hour session during which time you will carry out lots of practical activities such as CPR and bandaging. In addition, you will learn the appropriate measures to take in a range of emergency situations. How much does the course cost? £25.00 plus VAT Contact us Occupational Health & Safety This course is now running in digital format only. Contact us British Sign Language This Level 1 course will provide you with a basic understanding of British Sign Language. By the end of the course, you will be able to: Decipher the narrations of simple information presented to you in BSL. Describe events, issues, or matters in BSL. Engage in simple conversation with individuals who are Deaf, both in social situations and in the workplace or at school/college. How do I complete the course? You will attend a weekly in person session between October 2023 and March 2024. The course for 2022/23 will take place Wednesdays, 5:30pm - 7:30pm. How much does the course cost? The cost of this course is dependant on numbers. If 15 students sign up to the course the cost is £175.00 per person. Included within this cost is all tuition and full access to the online course enabling you time to practice BSL in your own time. You have the option to undertake an assessment at the end of the course for £115.00 Express an interest BSL Level 1 Contact us Institute of Leadership & Management We have teamed up with one of the UK’s leading leadership development organisations to provide you with the opportunity to excel in leadership and management. 
                        By undertaking these courses, you will improve your leadership skills and become more self-aware of your abilities to lead others and have all the essential knowledge to make change happen effectively. The courses available include: Leading Authentically: Self Awareness, Building Trust and Personal Branding. Further info here: Leading Authentically . Leading Strategically: Leading Change, Adaptability Leadership, Leading Projects. Further info here: Leading Strategically . How do I complete the course? You can choose either or both of the above short courses and study in your own time to complete online. How much does the course cost? Leading Authentically: £29 plus VAT Leading Strategically: £29 plus VAT Contact us The Cardiff Award This award is a structured framework that offers recognition for your career journey. Find out more Academic study skills These classes help students develop skills in topics like essay writing, revision, exam tips and note taking. Find out more Frequently asked questions What are the conditions for attending First Aid courses? We expect you to arrive at least 5 minutes before a course session is due to begin. If you are unable to attend a course on the day, please email fastwales@hotmail.co.uk as soon as possible and mark the subject line “From Cardiff student”. If you are unable to attend and do not advise us before the course starts, you will lose your course fee. If you do advise us before the course, we will look to transfer you to another date subject to availability. If you subsequently cannot attend a later date and have advised us before the course, we will consider a refund. To get the most out of the course, we advise that you actively participate in all the activities. When I tried to book a 1st aid course it appears full. Can I still attend? No, the course is sold out and subject to the maximum number permitted. Please book onto an alternative date. How do I cancel my place on the course? Please email Firstaidcourses@cardiff.ac.uk as soon as you become aware that you can’t attend the course. If you do advise us before the course, we will look to transfer you to another date subject to availability. If you subsequently cannot attend a later date and have advised us before the course, we will consider a refund. I have already graduated; can I still attend courses? We recognise the value students made to the university while studying and appreciate the roles of alumni.  If your student ID card still works, book as if you are still studying. If it has expired, please contact Firstaidcourses@cardiff.ac.uk . I am taking part in a course as part of a sports club or society. How do I book? Contact Firstaidcourses@cardiff.ac.uk with the following information: Club or Society name, your name, the number of students attending and preferred date(s).  Fees will be debited from your club or society account. Is there a text/exam in the course? The course does not involve an official test although you will be continually assessed by the instructor throughout the course by direct observation and questioning. How soon after completing will I receive my certificate? Usually about 10 days later. This will be emailed to you in e-format. How long is the certificate valid for? Three years from the completion date. Right to Work Checks Gwiriadau Hawl i Weithio A Right to Work check, or pre-employment check, is a legal check that must be completed by your employer before starting any paid work or work-related training in the UK. Mae gwiriad Hawl i Weithio neu wiriad cyn cyflogi, yn wiriad cyfreithiol rhaid i’ch cyflogwr ei gwblhau cyn i chi ddechrau unrhyw waith neu hyfforddiant taledig yn y DU. How does it work? When you complete a Right to Work check with Jobshop you will be issued with a Student Casual Worker Permit.  Without  one of these permits you cannot start any work or related training with Jobshop. If you have work arranged but don't yet have your Student Casual Worker Permit , please contact Jobshop immediately: Jobshopforms@cardiff.ac.uk . Please note, all UK/Irish students must attend the Right to Work check in person at the Jobshop office, these are by appointment only. Appointments should take no longer than 10 minutes. Ar Ôl Eich Shifftiau Finding Work | Canfod Gwaith How can I sign up to Jobshop? Firstly, you will need to create an account on the Jobshop portal. You can then set your preferences, sign up for job alerts and browse/ apply for jobs. Please note that you MUST complete your Right to Work check BEFORE starting any work or related training with Jobshop. This is a legal requirement stipulated by the Home Office. How can I contact Jobshop? You can email us on Jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk or call us on 02920 781535. I’m on a Student Visa, why do I need to send term dates when completing my Right to Work Check? Where can I find a copy of my term dates? Students on a Student Visa are limited to 10 or 20 hours work per week (Monday - Sunday) during term time. The Home Office request employers keep a copy of your term dates as part of the Right to Work documentation, to ensure you do not work over this limit when in term time. When completing your Right to Work check with us, please send a copy of your term dates clearly showing the start and end dates of your Christmas/Easter/Summer breaks (where applicable) along with your other Right to Work documents. Please note that this is different to your weekly lecture timetable. Undergraduates – please find guidance here which you can screenshot and email to us. If your course has non-standard term dates (e.g. MEDIC/ HCARE courses, placement years etc.), please send a copy of your term dates available in your course handbook or ask your school for an official copy. Postgraduate Taught – You may find a copy of your term dates in your module handbook. Alternatively, please contact your PG hub / course administrator / module leader / personal tutor and ask for an official document confirming your term dates. It must clearly show the start and end dates of your Christmas/Easter/Summer breaks (where applicable). If you have a dissertation or summer project, this counts as term time and needs to be outlined on your term dates. Please note, you cannot use the dates from the intranet link. Postgraduate Research – Please let us know in your email that you are a PGR student and therefore do not have set term time & recess periods. How do I renew my Jobshop Student Casual Worker Permit? We are required by the University to re-check all students’ Right to Work on an annual basis (or sooner if your Right to Work documents expire). To renew your Jobshop permit, please see guidance below: UK Students – Please send an email to jobshopforms@cardiff.ac.uk with a picture of your student card (or Proof of Enrolment letter, which you can download as a PDF document via your SIMS account) and we will update your permit for you. Irish Students – Please email jobshopforms@cardiff.ac.uk with a copy of your passport or passport card, Student ID card (or Proof of Enrolment letter, which you can download as a PDF document via your SIMS account). Settled / Pre-Settled Students – Please email jobshopforms@cardiff.ac.uk with a copy of your passport, Student ID card (or Proof of Enrolment letter, which you can download as a PDF document via your SIMS account) and your online ‘share code’ which is available from the Gov.uk website: https://www.gov.uk/prove-right-to-work . Please see here for more information on the Right to Work check. VISA Students – Please email jobshopforms@cardiff.ac.uk with a copy of your BRP card (Front and Back), Student ID card (or Proof of Enrolment letter, which you can download as a PDF document via your SIMS account) and a copy of your term dates (if applicable). You will also need your online ‘share code’ which is available from the Gov.uk website: https://www.gov.uk/prove-right-to-work . Please see here for more information on the Right to Work check. How many hours can I work each week? The university advises that students on full-time courses of study, work no more than 15 hours per week during term-time. Students with a Student Visa are restricted to either 10 or 20 hours work per week during term time (details are shown on your BRP/ visa letter) and must not exceed their visa allowances under any circumstances. More detailed advice is available from UKCISA . Students on funded courses of study may have further restrictions, please check your individual guidance on this. What documents do I need to provide for my Right to Work check? Click here for more information on the documents we need prior to organising the Right to Work check. I am waiting for a new Biometric Residence Permit/visa, what do I do? If you are in the process of getting a new visa/BRP and you have been asked to work, we can complete a check with the Home Office while you wait for your documents to be returned. To do this you will need to get in touch with Jobshop. You will not be able to work until this ECS check has been returned. ECS stands for Employer Checking Service. An employer can use the government website to confirm if a person is in the process of applying for a new or replacement visa document. Once this is confirmed & we have completed your Right to Work check you will be able to work. What is a National Insurance number? How do I apply for one? Your National Insurance number makes sure that the National Insurance contributions and tax you pay are properly recorded against your name. It also acts as a reference number when communicating with the Department for Work and Pensions and HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC). To apply for a National Insurance Number, please visit gov.uk/apply-national-insurance-number . If you need to update your NINO, please email Jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk from your university email address with your NINO details. Can I work through Jobshop if I am no longer a student? Students are typically eligible to work through Jobshop for three months after your end of studies date, which is the expiry date shown on your student ID card/ Proof of Enrolment letter. I’m on a Student Visa, can I work full-time during vacation periods? Your shifts | Eich Shifftiau What if I need to cancel a placement/ shift? You MUST be sure of your availability before applying for a job. Once you have accepted a job, you are committed to working and cancellation is only acceptable in the case of sickness or an emergency. If this is the case, please contact Jobshop via email or call as soon as possible. If you need to cancel a shift outside of Jobshop office hours, please contact the employer directly. You will find contact information in your placement confirmation email. Occasionally work may be cancelled due to circumstances beyond our control. We are unable to offer payment in such cases. What are the working restrictions for Student Visa holders? Students with a student visa are restricted in the number of hours they can work each week during term-time. Your eligibility to work will be outlined on your BRP card, and/or in your visa decision letter. As postgraduate-research (PhD) students do not have fixed term dates, the university stipulates that their working restriction should apply all year round. If you are studying in the UK on a visitor visa you are not permitted to work at any time, including unpaid/voluntary work. Can I work from outside the UK? Please be aware that we are unable to facilitate remote working whilst overseas. The legal requirements of working remotely overseas can be highly complex for both workers and employers, and we would be unable to guarantee that individual workers would not have to pay tax or social security bills in other countries. What are the expectations of me whilst at work? Please remember you are representing Cardiff University and Cardiff Students’ Union whilst on your work placement. You are expected to complete the work to the best of your ability and follow the particulars agreed to in the Student Casual Worker Agreement (Jobshop contract). We ask managers to provide clear instructions to all staff and to set the expectations of the role from the outset. Where possible, we ask this to be provided in writing, however in some posts this will not be feasible and requirements may be discussed verbally. If you are unsure of your responsibilities, please speak to your line manager in the first instance.  If you are having any issues with your placement, please contact jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk . If you are working remotely (in the UK), you are expected to be available and completing work during the agreed shift time. You should agree expected output, how to share work and deadlines with your line manager. Am I entitled to a break whilst at work? Everyone is entitled to a 20 minute rest break for every 6 hours worked. If you have worked over 6 hours and not received a break, please raise this with your line manager. Typically, breaks are unpaid, your line manager will let you know if there is any variation to this and if you should include breaks on your timesheet or not. If you are on a student visa, please be aware that the total amount of hours claimed on your timesheet is what will count towards your working restriction, so please keep this in mind if you are being paid for breaks. Beth os oes angen i mi ganslo lleoliad/shifft? RHAID i chi wirio eich argaeledd cyn ymgeisio ar gyfer swydd. Unwaith i chi dderbyn swydd rydych chi wedi ymrwymo i weithio ac mae canslo ond yn dderbyniol mewn achosion argyfwng neu oherwydd salwch. Os taw dyma’r achos, e-bostiwch neu ffoniwch y Siopswyddi cyn gynted â phosib. Os oes angen i chi ganslo shifft tu allan i oriau gwaith y Siopswyddi, cysylltwch yn uniongyrchol gyda’ch cyflogwr. Gallwch ddod o hyd i’w manylion cyswllt yn eich e-bost cadarnhau lleoliad. Weithiau, efallai y bydd gwaith yn cael ei ganslo oherwydd amgylchiadau tu allan i’n rheolaeth. Ni allwn gynnig tâl yn y fath achosion. Beth yw’r cyfyngiadau gwaith ar fyfyrwyr gyda fisa? Mae’r nifer o oriau gall myfyrwyr gyda fisa eu gweithio bob wythnos wedi’u cyfyngu yn ystod y tymor. Bydd eich Hawl i Weithio wedi’i amlinellu ar eich cerdyn BRP a/neu yn eich llythyr fisa. Fel myfyriwr ymchwil ôl-raddedig (PhD) heb ddyddiadau tymor penodol, mae’r brifysgol yn datgan bod cyfyngiadau yn berthnasol trwy’r flwyddyn. Os ydych yn astudio yn y DU ar fisa ymwelydd nid oes hawl gennych weithio ar unrhyw adeg, gan gynnwys gwaith di-dâl/gwirfoddol. A allaf weithio o du allan i’r DU? Ni allwn hwyluso gwaith o bell tra byddwch dramor. Mae’r gofyniadau cyfreithiol ar gyfer gwaith o bell tra thramor yn hynod gymhleth ar gyfer gweithwyr a chyflogwyr, a ni fydden yn gallu gwarantu na fyddai rhaid i weithwyr dalu treth neu ffioedd nawdd cymdeithasol mewn gwledydd eraill. Beth yw’r disgwyliadau ohonof wrth weithio? Cofiwch, rydych yn cynrychioli Prifysgol Caerdydd ac Undeb Myfyrwyr Caerdydd tra’n gweithio. Mae disgwyl i chi gwblhau’r gwaith i orau eich gallu a dilyn y telerau wedi’u gosod yn y Cytundeb Gwaith Dros Dro (cytundeb y Siopswyddi). Rydym yn gofyn rheolwyr i ddarparu cyfarwyddiadau clir i staff a gosod disgwyliadau o’r dechrau. Lle’n bosib, rydym yn gofyn iddynt ddarparu hyn yn ysgrifenedig, ond mewn rhai amgylchiadau ni fydd hyn yn bosib a bydd gofynion yn cael eu trafod ar lafar. Os ydych yn ansicr am eich cyfrifoldebau, siaradwch gyda’ch rheolwr llinell yn gyntaf. Os ydych yn cael problemau ar eich lleoliad, cysylltwch â jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk . Os ydych yn gweithio o bell (yn y DU), mae disgwyl i chi fod ar gael a’n cwblhau eich gwaith yn ystod yr amser shifft perthnasol. Dylech gytuno ar allbwn disgwyliedig, sut i rannu gwaith, a therfynau amser gyda’ch rheolwr llinell. Ydw i’n gymwys i gael egwyl yn ystod gwaith? Mae hawl gan bawb gymryd egwyl o 20 munud ar gyfer pob 6 awr maent yn gweithio. Os ydych wedi gweithio dros 6 awr a heb dderbyn egwyl, codwch hyn gyda’ch rheolwr llinell. Fel arfer, ni fyddwch yn derbyn tâl yn ystod eich egwyl, ond bydd eich rheolwr llinell yn rhoi gwybod i chi os yw hyn yn wahanol ac os ddylech gynnwys seibiau ar eich taflen amser neu beidio. Os ydych ar fisa myfyriwr, byddwch yn ymwybodol y bydd y nifer o oriau ar eich taflen amser yn cyfrif tuag at eich cyfyngiad gwaith, felly cadwch hyn mewn cof os ydych yn derbyn tâl am egwylion. After your shifts | Ar Ôl Eich Shifftiau When do I get paid? Wages are paid fortnightly in arrears on alternate Fridays. Check out our Instagram highlights here to see upcoming paydays. How much will I be paid? This will vary depending on where you are working and the job you are doing, but all jobs through Jobshop are paid at a minimum of the current National Living Wage rate. The hourly rate of pay will always be included on the job advertisement and your offer of work. How do I complete and submit my timesheet? Once you have a firm offer of work and have completed your onboarding, your timesheets will be available to view and complete on the Jobshop candidate portal before they are sent to your line manager for authorisation. You can select the timesheet from the ‘incomplete / not submitted section’ in the timesheet widget. We suggest you fill this in at the end of the week (on a Sunday) as you only get one timesheet per role, per week. Here you will be able to input the start and end time of your shifts, and you will see a total amount of hours in the ‘time worked’ section. Please check that this is correct and then submit your timesheet. Your timesheets will automatically become available for each week of your placement and will stop when you reach the end date. If your placement has been extended and you no longer have timesheets available, please contact jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk from your university email address and include the full name of the role that you are missing timesheets for. Please be aware that timesheets are only available on your Jobshop account for 6 months. We ask that you submit timesheets promptly after completing any work. If timesheets are not submitted within 6 months, we might not be able to process payment. How can I access my payslip? Once your wages have been processed, you will be emailed a link to view your payslips within the Sage app. What is a P45/P60 and how do I get one? A P45 is a certificate given to an employee at the end of a period of employment, providing details of their tax code, gross pay, and the tax paid for that year which is to be passed to a subsequent employer or benefit agency. Please note we will not be able to issue you with your P45 until you have received your final payment from Jobshop as the process removes you from our payroll – please only email to request this once you have received your final payment. If you require your P45, please email us at Jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk . A P60 (End of Year Certificate) is a statement issued to taxpayers at the end of a tax year. This will be available on the Sage app automatically at the end of each tax year (around April) if you have worked for us during that tax year. I have changed my address, what do I do? Please email your new address to Jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk from your university email address. We will update the payroll with your new details. I have changed my bank details, what do I do? Please email Jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk and request a change of bank details form. We will update the payroll with your new details. What is your General Data Protection Policy? Employers Hiring Manager Portal Porth Rheolwyr Cyflogi Recruiting via Jobshop Recriwtio trwy’r Siopswyddi If you would like to recruit student staff through Jobshop, you must first be set up on our system as a Hiring Manager and register your vacancy by completing a Vacancy Requisition Form. Os hoffech recriwtio staff sy’n fyfyrwyr trwy’r Siopswyddi, yn gyntaf rhaid cofrestru ar gyfer ein system fel Rheolwr Cyflogi a chreu swydd wag trwy gwblhau’r Ffurflen Swydd Wag. I’m a new hiring manager If you are not already set up on our system as a Hiring Manager: please contact us at Jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk so that we can arrange this. Please include your full name, Cardiff University email address, and job title as you would like these to appear on our system. I’m already set up as a hiring manager Please log into your account here using your Cardiff email and complete a Vacancy Requisition Form to start the recruitment process. Please note that all Jobshop Vacancy Requisition Forms must be accompanied by the relevant Kenexa approval (in line with the current university recruitment controls). Find out more about this here . Once you have completed a Vacancy Requisition Form with details of your vacancy, it will be advertised on our jobs page (unless you have notified us that you have already identified a suitable candidate and therefore don’t need to advertise it). Students will then be able to apply online. You can choose from the following recruitment processes: View all applications for your vacancy View a shortlist of applications for your vacancy Ask the Jobshop to recruit and select a suitable candidate on your behalf Ask students to apply via a website link None of the above (as you have already identified a suitable student/s) Please note that you must raise a Vacancy Requisition on the Jobshop system even if you have already identified a suitable student for your vacancy. This will enable us to make sure the student you wish to employ has a current Right to Work check in place before they start work and will allow us to complete the on-boarding process (i.e. gather the new starter information in order to generate electronic timesheets for the student and process their wages). Find our current rates here . Your responsibilities as a hiring manager The Vacancy Requisition Form, Right to Work Check and onboarding processes must all be fully completed before a student is permitted to start any work or related training. It is the responsibility of the employing staff member to ensure that the above process has been followed. Once a student has completed their Right to Work check, they will be issued with a Jobshop Student Casual Worker Permit (also known as a Jobshop permit). You must ask to see this permit before you allow a student to start work, and check that it is in-date. Please note, students can be registered on our website and not have completed the legal pre-employment check. Reminder: as an employer, we have a duty to prevent illegal working and failure to conduct Right to Work checks BEFORE A STUDENT COMMENCES WORK means that the University may breach Home Office regulations. Managers who fail to ensure a Right to Work check has been conducted before work is undertaken risk being subject to disciplinary action and personal liability for any fines incurred as a result. If you are employing an international student on a student visa, please remind them that they must ensure the TOTAL number of hours they work each week between Monday-Sunday does not exceed the limit shown on their visa or BRP (which will also be noted on their permit). This must include any voluntary work as well as paid work completed through Jobshop and other employers. If you are managing a role in which you are responsible for authorising timesheets, you need to ensure these are authorised by the deadline of 2pm each Monday to prevent any delays in payment to students. Find out more here . Frequently Asked Questions Cwestiynau Cyffredin How do I access the Hiring Manager Portal? Hiring Manager Portal Please login using your Cardiff email and the password you set up when first accessing the system. If you are struggling to access your account, please email jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk . What is recruitment approval? All Jobshop Vacancy Requisition Forms must be accompanied by the relevant recruitment approval (in line with the current university recruitment controls). Recruitment approval will need to be obtained using the university's systems internally by your department. Please contact your local HR or finance team to begin this process. Please note, we cannot process roles with a requisition ‘pending’ approval. What is a budget/finance code? Before you submit your vacancy, you will need to obtain a 3-part Oracle allocation code from your local Finance Department or budget holder. Please enter this in the three fields provided (if you are using a research/ project code, which only has one part, please populate the second field with the code).  Please see an example below - the 10-digit analysis code should be two letters followed by 8 numbers, the 5-digit cost centre code will be the first 5 numbers of the analysis code, and the allocation code will always be ‘10711’ for ‘Unistaff Jobshop Temporary Staff’. Cost Centre (5): 12345 Analysis (10): AB12345678 Unistaff Allocation (5): 10711 If you have a research/project code, this will be 6 digits and should be entered in the second box (10-digit space). If your code needs to be changed on an existing vacancy, please contact Jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk . What is a Student Casual Worker Permit/ Jobshop Card? Jobshop issue Student Casual Worker Permits (also known as a Jobshop permit) as a locked digital PDF once students have completed their pre-employment checks with the team. You must ask to see this permit before you allow a student to start work. This is what proves they have completed the necessary legal checks for work and states any visa restrictions (if applicable). How long can I employ students through Jobshop post-graduation? Students can work through Jobshop for 3-months post their end of study date (as stated on their student card/Proof of Enrolment letter). We do not use the date they receive results or have their graduation ceremony. For PhD students who have variable course end dates, we can typically allow students to work for 3-months from the date of their viva. If you wish to continue their employment after this point, please speak to your local HR Manager. What are the Jobshop pay rates and costs? Our current hourly charges are as follows (the example given is based on the current ‘Real’ Living Wage of £13.45 per hour although you can pay a higher rate if you wish). £13.45 (basic hourly rate) + 12.07% (holiday pay) = £15.07 per hour (paid to the student) Plus £1.15 (administration charge) = £16.22 per hour* *plus Employer's National Insurance contributions, NEST pension contributions and other associated payroll costs, e.g. Statutory Sick Pay (if applicable). The employer rate for NI is 15% of earnings over £96 per week for staff aged over 21, or 15% of earnings over £967 per week for staff aged under 21 NEST employer pension contributions are payable at 3% of earnings over the Lower Earnings Limit of £120 per week only (and then only if the employee is a member of NEST) Rates must come through to Jobshop as an hourly rate, rather than a grade-point scale. How do I approve timesheets? Hiring Manager Portal Students will complete and submit their timesheets in the Candidate Portal at the end of each week. Once a student has submitted a timesheet, the relevant Hiring Manager(s) will receive a notification. Please ensure that you authorise any outstanding timesheets for the previous week before the weekly deadline of 14:00 on Monday to avoid payroll delays. Once in the Hiring Manager portal, you’ll need to click on the timesheet icon (the clock symbol) on the left-hand side of the Hiring Manager dashboard and you’ll see any timesheets awaiting authorisation. Click on the date on the left-hand side and this will take you into the timesheet. Scroll down to where it says, ‘Authorise Timesheet’, check the box next to ‘Please tick to authorise this timesheet’ and click ‘Save’. If you disagree with the number of hours submitted, you can reject the timesheet, adding a message to the student with details of your query. Please click the reject button after leaving a comment, and then confirm this in the pop-up box. If a timesheet is incorrect, please reject this to send it back to the student – it is much harder to edit or recall a timesheet once it has been authorised. If a student is struggling with accessing or submitting timesheets, please ask the student to contact jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk directly. How do I become a Hiring Manager? If you are not already set up on our system as a Hiring Manager, please contact us at jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk so that we can arrange this. Please include your full name, Cardiff University email address, and job title as you would like these to appear on our system. We will need to gain authorisation from your department to add you to the system and give you the relevant recruitment permissions. How do I check if a student is registered and/or Right to Work checked? Please note, students who have registered on the portal have not necessarily completed the legal pre-employment (Right to Work) checks. You can check if a student has a valid Right to Work check by asking to see their Jobshop Student Casual Worker Permit. This will show the expiry date of their check and any work restrictions they may have. If the student cannot produce this permit and you need to check their Right to Work status, or whether they have created an account on the Candidate Portal, send an email to jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk , quote the students full-name and Cardiff University email address, and we can check this for you. How do I add students to an existing role? If you are managing an existing role with Jobshop and need to add students onto this role, please email jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk requesting this, and quote the vacancy number, student name and their Cardiff University email address. Please ensure your budget and Kenexa cover additional students being added before requesting this. How do I extend a current role? If you are managing an existing role and the end date of a placement or vacancy needs to be extended, please email jobshop@cardiff.ac.uk requesting this. In the body of the email quote the vacancy number, student name and their Cardiff University email address, and the date that this needs to be extended to. Please ensure your budget and Kenexa cover additional students being added before requesting this. If a new Kenexa or budget/finance code are required, please include these in your request. University Staff Employers There are some really exciting things going on in the Students’ Union in Freshers 2025 and we want you to help us make it happen! As part of this project, we’re looking for friendly, enthusiastic people to join the Welcome Team to introduce over 6,000 new students to the University. Joining the Welcome Team is an amazing opportunity to volunteer your time to make a huge difference to the student experience, make loads of friends and acquire new skills that will stay with you forever. You’ll also make a huge positive impact on your CV while doing it. What are you commiting to? Joining the Welcome Team is a totally manageable commitment. We recognise that you'll have other things going on in Freshers. We ask everyone on the team to: Give 15 - 20 hours of flexible shift commitment during Freshers. Be available for training on the 16th September. Show enthusiasm and passion for the Students' Union, the student experience and student welfare. Be present on campus the week of Freshers'. What will you be doing? We're asking for 15 - 20 hours of your time in September to help us make Freshers 2025. You'll be able to get involved with: Welcoming new students to Cardiff SU. Supporting and/or leading Give it a Go Trips and Tours. Helping our full-time staff at the Sports Fairs and Societies & Volunteering Fairs. Promoting all of our Give it a Go activities to students across campus. Championing our support and welfare services. Promoting all of the fantastic services, events and activities that we offer. Telling everyone how amazing the Students’ Union is! What's in it for you? You’ll be welcomed into the Students’ Union Family and become an integral and valued part of our exciting Freshers' plans.  As well as a warm feeling on the inside, you’ll also get: A position of responsibility. A branded t-shirt and lanyard. An accredited Students’ Union Certificate of Contribution; The chance to meet new like-minded people. Training from experienced Students’ Union staff; An extra CV reference! Person Specification Role Description Apply Now! Cardiff Student Union! You Can Contact SU Finance via: Email : SUFinance@cardiff.ac.uk Phone : 029 2078 1445 You can also come to see us at the Finance Office on the 3 rd floor of the Students’ Union, just down the corridor from the Activities Department. We are open Monday to Friday, 10am to 4pm . Please see the information below to learn more about how our services work, along with signposts to other services that may be helpful to you. Our Services If you have any questions about ticket or membership purchases made through the Students' Union website, our Finance Team is here to help. We can assist with: Queries about transactions Provide information Support you with refund requests If you are a committee member and are looking for guidance on your group’s finances, please go to the committee resources finance section. Refunds Refunds for a product sold by a club/society: Refunds can only be processed at committee discretion therefore you would need to get in touch with the committee and request a refund. The committee would then need to get in contact with SU Finance providing the student number of the student who requires a refund and the product that needs refunding. We will be in touch once the refund has been processed. Refunds for events sold on the SU website: Tickets have individual refund policies, and this is at the discretion of the seller. Please email us if you require a refund and we will forward this on to the relevant department. If approved, we will be in touch to let you know that this has been processed. Unable to purchase something on the SU website due to error message Membership errors: If you cannot checkout due to membership errors, email us at SUFinance@cardiff.ac.uk . Please provide your student number and a screenshot of the error. Transaction errors: First, please ensure that the billing address you enter matches the one registered to your payment card, as any mismatch may result in an error message. If the issue continues, you’re welcome to purchase the product in person at the Finance Office. If visiting in person isn’t possible, simply send us an email with details of the product you're trying to purchase. We’ll then be able to send you a personalised payment link to complete your transaction online. Advice Topics Academic Complaints Student Life Housing Health & Wellbeing Emergency Contacts Postgrad Research Students International Students Healthcare Students Advice Operating Policies Confidentiality Statement Student Advice is committed to providing confidential advice, information and support. Student Advice is committed to providing advice and information on a range of issues that relate to students’ academic, welfare and general advice needs. Student Advice is a confidential and independent service. If you are concerned about disclosing information in our reception area please ask to speak to someone in private. Student Advice does not share the information you give us with other individuals and/or organisations outside of Cardiff University Students' Union without your express permission except in very exceptional circumstances; for example, if we believe that you or other people are at risk of serious harm. Customer Care Statement The Student Advice service is one that is committed to providing strictly confidential, neutral and non-prejudice support and guidance. We see every student as an individual and treat each student with respect and dignity as these are the core values within our service. With approachable staff, we pride ourselves on providing a warm, friendly and open minded service. Each adviser strives to achieve the best possible outcome for every student, whether it be looking for housing or an academic appeal. Intertwined within our core values is our confidentiality agreement. This ensures that all students who use our service are provided with the upmost discretion. We provide support in a number of areas and tackle each problem with a ‘can do’ attitude. However, we will be honest and transparent if we do not believe it is possible to achieve the desired outcome. With our core values in mind, we endeavour to support students to help themselves through their time at university. Withdrawal of Services Policy Student Advice delivers free, independent, confidential, impartial advice to students at Cardiff University. There will be situations where it is no longer appropriate / a justifiable use of resource / safe to continue to provide assistance to a student. In these circumstances students will be signposted or referred on to another agency. This can be done after discussion with the Head of Student Advice or Director. If an adviser feels, despite the information and resources available, that Student Advice is not the appropriate agency, the student will be provided with active signposting. Student Advice will routeinly refer students to University Student Support, if they are the more appropriate source of advice. The following is a non-exhaustive list of where service may be withdrawn: The student is violent or abusive There is a potential of fraud There has been a loss of confidence The potential user is not a priority / target group The student has not taken any action and returns to the service repeating the original inquiry Student presents to Student Advice repeatedly without any real advice needs The student is being threatening, or the Adviser feels threatened The student has given false and/or misleading information to Student Advice. The relationship is no longer that of client and adviser The nature of the case changes and this change means that Student Advice is no longer appropriate or the best source of advice The student transfers to another University The students’ behaviour is in breach of our Equal Opportunities policy The student has seriously breached the trust of staff e.g. theft from Student Advice Verbal abuse, or perceived threats to members of the Student Advice team, will never be tolerated. Where Student Advice's service is being withdrawn, the client will be informed verbally and if possible in writing, with the reason(s) why this is the case, with suggestions of where else they can seek help and informing them of their right to complain if they feel this action has been taken unreasonably.
